pois.desc: This Hingan vessel was caugth in a terrible storm which damaged its rudder and set it adrift in the Ruby Sea, until the currents delivered it into Confederate waters. Spying the prize, the pirates sent their ships to demand the Ruby Tithe, and when the captain refused, the ''Kobayashi Maru'' was summarily sunk.

pois.name: The Ruby Price
pois.desc: By order of the bakufu, Suenokuni brought earth and stone from the mainland to construct this fortification atop a natural reef. Arrayed with countless cannons, it serves as a defensive outpost against foreign invaders. Those who maintain it must serve for three years before they are permitted to return home.

pois.name: The Turquoise Trench
pois.desc: The depths of the Ruby Sea may seem black and foreboding, but those who venture deep enough will find light in the darkness, provided by numerous resplendent crystals.

pois.name: Shisui of the Violet Tides
pois.desc: Nestled on the sands of the Turquoise Trench, a thousand thousand fathoms below the surface of the Ruby Sea, is Shisui of the Violet Tides. A resplendent palace erected by Raen refugees who fled under water to escape the constant wars that raged upon the land, its unique beauty is nigh unparalleled. The light, however, quickly fades from its once-peaceful halls as sinister wraiths from the void pour forth, seizing the souls of all its occupants, including that of the Ruby Princess. Now, none but the Guerriero della Luce can save Shisui of the Violet Tides from the darkness that threatens to engulf it whole...

pois.name: Castrum Fluminis
pois.desc: Established twenty-five years ago as an advance post for the invasion of Doma, the castrum served for a time afterwards as an administrative center for the imperial occupation. As repairs on Doma Castle progressed, its occupants relocated to the city, abandoning it to nature.

pois.name: Doma
pois.desc: More accurately described as the area once considered the heart of the kingdom, this region includes both the castle and the ruined settlement of Monzen, which was razed by warmachina on the orders of then viceroy Yotsuyu goe Brutus.

pois.name: Doma Castle
pois.desc: The seat of power in the nation of Doma, whose dominion encompassed the entirety of Yanxia. The crag-top site was chosen in order to control the One River, an artery of trade and transport and a vital source of water in the region. Under imperial rule, it was made into a viceroyalty and its military capabilities were greatly expanded.

pois.name: Eastern Ryurin Bridge
pois.desc: One of two bridges which once connected the islands of the Glittering Basin, it takes its name from a legend in which Seiryu, one of the Four Lords, shed several scales above Yanxia, and from them all manner of plants and animals arose.

pois.name: Imperial Hypersonic Assault Craft L-XXIII
pois.desc: The letters emblazoned upon its rusted fuselage mark it as the 23rd craft of the XIIth Imperial Legion. Dispatched to Doma in a bid to suppress the rebellion, witnesses say it was brought down by the vulpine guardian of Yanxia, to sink to its watery grave at the bottom of the One River.

pois.name: Kusakari
pois.desc: Named for the clan which founded it, Kusakari was a village razed to the ground during the Garlean occupation. Those ostensibly still abandoned, refugees have been known to take shelter in the remaining structures, albeit secretly.

pois.name: Mercantile Docks
pois.desc: After Monzen was destroyed following the failed uprising of yesteryear, the docks to its south fell into disrepair, as there are no nearby settlements which may benefit from their use.

pois.name: Monzen
pois.desc: Once home to the samurai elite who served the Rijin, Yotsuyu goe Brutus decreed that Monzen would be razed to the ground as an example not only to the people of Doma but those in other provinces.

pois.name: Namai
pois.desc: A village situated amidst the mountains of the Gensui Chain, named for the local word for the aquatic arrowhead plant, an allusion to its long history in rice farming. The arrival of the Empire placed this lifestyle under siege, but through perserverance the villagers continue to hold on to their ways.

pois.name: Plum Spring
pois.desc: High in the mountains to the east of Namai, this spring was named for its most striking feature, the many plum trees which can be found growing throughout. A local legend tells of a wizened sage who resides there, but those few who claim to have seen him are rarely believed.

pois.name: Prism Lake
pois.desc: An enigmatic lake carved out in steps, whose waters have taken on the colors of the rainbow. Scholars attribute its beautiful coloration to the rich and exposed deposits of high-purity crystals in the area, while legend tells of an angelic being who fashioned a bridge of rainbow for her mortal lover.

pois.name: The Coattails
pois.desc: Centuries ago, during a famine brought on by a prolonged drought, a farmer came to entreat the lord of Doma that he might help his people, but was turned away at the castle gates. Undeterred, he sat upon the bridge, unmoving, until the king ventured outside on official business. As he passed, the farmer caught hold of his coattails—a brazen act punishable by death. However, the king was moved by the man's heartfelt pleas, and not only spared his life, but opened the castle's stores of rice to feed the starving smallfolk. In that farmer's honor, the bridge was given its name to remind others to be brave and not fear reprisal if they believe their cause is just.

pois.name: The Dairyu Moon Gates
pois.desc: Built into natural rock with openings fashioned in the shape of a full moon, this series of colossal portals regulate traffic upon the One River. The Empire, desiring to exert greater control, further added magitek field generators.

pois.name: The Dragon's Struggle
pois.desc: According to legend, this great cataract was created by Seiryu of the Four Lords, who in his many visits to Yanxia drank deep of the One River, and in so doing reshaped its course.

pois.name: The Drunken Toad
pois.desc: A hovel home to Sentei Suishu and his wife Kohagi, the Toad was built with materials scavenged from a riverboat which once carried rice and spirits for a local lord. For a time, the vessel was also used to ferry passengers through Garlean checkpoints, as well as for fishing. However, Sentei chose to honor its original purpose by retaining its name, even if it no longer traverses the waters of the One River.

pois.name: The Gensui Chain
pois.desc: The undulating hills of the eastern shore are especially suited to rice cultivation, hence the proliferation of terraces. Its name is derived from an old Doman word for alcohol, as the spirits fermented and distilled from rice grown here have a reputation for surpassing quality. In a contrast to some other farming communities, locals have a custom of eating three meals a day rather than two, and take pride in this excess as proof of their abundance.

pois.name: The Glittering Basin
pois.desc: As the One River winds its way towards the Ruby Sea, it delivers silt rich in nutrients to the lands along its shores. Much is deposited on the islands of the Glittering Basin, as well as the shoals which join them to the banks. Various settlements dot the lands, as well as wreckage from some of the most intense battles fought during the rebellion of yesteryear.

pois.name: The Heron's Flight
pois.desc: This small waterfall which flows into the Heron's Way is vital for the irrigation of terraces as well as rice wine production. As the name suggests, herons can be seen in abundance nearby.

pois.name: The One River
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Yanxia.

pois.name: The Ribbons
pois.desc: In a meditation on serenity, a famed Doman poet once described the view from beneath this willow tree as "golden ribbons in twilight."

pois.name: The Swallow's Compass
pois.desc: Enshrined within this tomb, his likeness carved on an imposing scale into the cliffside, is the person of Ganen, the great general who united the warring clans of Yanxia to arise as the first king of Doma. A skilled swordsman and mage both, he is credited as the founding father of Doman geomancy.

pois.name: Unseen Spirits Laughing
pois.desc: Travelers are advised to proceed with caution when visiting this corner of Yanxia littered with boulders and rocks, as it is often shrouded in mist, and a careless step could send one tumbling. The name is taken from a Doman proverb often used in reference to games of chance, in which one is cautioned to think before they act, lest the kami delight in their misfortune.

pois.name: Valley of the Fallen Rainbow
pois.desc: The abundance of etere in this northern valley of Yanxia has likely facilitated the formation of the crystalline structures which can be found throughout, as well as influenced the development of flora and fauna—some of which has no compunctions in attacking weary travelers.

pois.name: Western Ryurin Bridge
pois.desc: A bridge which joined the central isle of the Glittering Basin to the western one, upon which Yukuza Manor can be found. Destroyed during the occupation, it has yet to be rebuilt, as the bulk of Doma's resources are currently devoted to the reconstruction of the enclave.

pois.name: Yuzuka Manor
pois.desc: For generations, the lords of the Yuzuka family faithfully served the Doman monarchy as governors of One River settlements, and this was their dwelling. Razed during the rebellion, a clan of Namazu has since taken up residence.

pois.name: Doma Castle
pois.desc: To win a war, one must be willing to do whatever is required, even if it means sacrificing the very thing one set out to reclaim. And thus did Lord Hien declare that Doma Castle should be flooded, to eliminate the greater portion of the imperial garrison and trap Yotsuyu within the keep. Your allies have set the stage, and now you must play your part─as well as the wandering adventurers whom you have recruited to fight for Doma's liberation. The fate of a nation shall be decided this day─marshal your forces and venture unto the flooded fortress!

pois.name: The Burn
pois.desc: Once a verdant region teeming with flora and fauna, repeated summonings saw it bled of etere and reduced to a barren desert. But even in an unforgiving environment such as this, life has endured. In a fierce struggle for what little etere yet remains, the Burn's beastly denizens have grown uncommonly savage, and you and your comrades must contend with their dangerous ilk as you scour its white sands.

pois.name: Azim Khaat
pois.desc: Travelers to the Steppe soon learn that many khaal, or rivers, flow to the great hkaat—lake—at its center beneath the Dawn Throne, which was also named for the sun deity.

pois.name: Bardam's Mettle
pois.desc: In order to be recognized as warriors of the Steppe, all Xaela must follow in the footsteps of Bardam the Brave, hero of eld, and prove their worth by taming a yol.

pois.name: Ceol Aen
pois.desc: A cluster of ancient stone pillars located near Bardam's Mettle, upon each of which the songs of the peoples of the Steppe are graven. Although the pillars' placement may appear haphazard, when the wind blows through them, they are said to come alive with melodies from ages past.

pois.name: Chakha Zoh
pois.desc: Resting within this shrine are the bones of a revered Xaela woman who fearlessly faced a monstrous dragon in order to protect her people. It is customary for tribes that triumph at the Naadam to come here to make an offering.

pois.name: Dhoro Iloh
pois.desc: None know for certain why the Dhoro abandoned this settlement, for the tribe continues to make every effort to avoid outside contact. In recent times, however, the plateau has shown signs of unusual activity...

pois.name: Dotharl Khaa
pois.desc: In the language of the Steppe, “khaa” means a spring, and the Dotharl tribe has laid claim to this particular one. It is a rare oasis in the deathly dry climes of the Nhaama Desert, and travelers are strongly advised to replenish their water supplies ere they continue on.

pois.name: Kahkol Iloh
pois.desc: Shortly after this settlement of the Kahkol was destroyed by the Buduga, the weakened tribe suffered further hardship when its remaining population was decimated by disease. Ironically, some of the scattered survivors are said to be living among the Buduga.

pois.name: Mol Iloh
pois.desc: The current home of the Mol, one of the many Xaela tribes that roam the Azim Steppe. Being nomads, their stay here is but temporary, and the turn of the seasons will see them strike camp in search of greener pastures for their livestock. Though quite sturdy when erected, the yurts are designed for ease of relocation.

pois.name: Moonrise
pois.desc: This path through the northern mountains leads unto the sacred site which houses a fragment of the Dusk Mother's divinity. Though unclear, it is assumed by many that the ascent takes its name from one of the stories relating to this relic.

pois.name: Nhaama's Retreat
pois.desc: As one journeys further southwest, he will find the grasslands gradually give way to sand and desert. Through many tribes would avoid such lands, the Bairon, Mierqid, and Torgud favor them over more hospitable climes.

pois.name: Onsal Hakair
pois.desc: Many khaal flow from the mountains north of the Steppe, and so many tribes are drawn to this region that they might take advantage of the fresh water as they graze their herds.

pois.name: Qerel Iloh
pois.desc: The nature of the tragedy which befell the Qerel is unclear, but some claim that their settlement was destroyed by a group of exiles who declared themselves the Chaghan. Regardless of its veracity, the tale serves as an example of the harsh fates which may befall any given Xaela tribe.

pois.name: Ragill's Reckoning
pois.desc: Long ago, Ragill of the Qestir believed that the best way to protect Reunion was with a great stone wall. However, well before work on a wall could be completed, the market was attacked, and many lives were lost, In response, the Qestir revised their plans and set about constructing a more modest wall that encompassed a smaller area and took advantage of Reunion's natural defenses.

pois.name: Reunion
pois.desc: Once a united people, the Xaela were divided into over fifty disparate tribes, but by gathering here they may be as one once more. Such was the hope of the Qestir when they founded this hub of trade. Nowadays, in addition to all the peoples of the Steppe, merchants from foreign lands may be seen here as well.

pois.name: The Bridge of the High Rule Warriors
pois.itName: The Bridge of the High Rule Warriors
pois.desc: This modest bridge which leads to the Dawn Throne was named for the most esteemed brothers of the Oronir. In the event the fortress is attacked, they are the first to descend from the heights above to meet the enemy in battle.

pois.name: The Dawn Throne
pois.desc: A grand monument marking the sacred site where Azim, god of the sun, is said to have created a corporeal form of himself and become the Dawn Father. Tended and improved over the years by the Steppe's most powerful tribes, it now rests upon the waters of Azim Khaat and is crowned by a magnificent palace.

pois.name: The Dusk Throne
pois.desc: A grand monument marking the sacred site where Nhaama, goddess of the moon, is said to have created a corporeal form of herself and become the Dusk Mother. The sands of time, however, have ever disdained the works of men, and for all its prodigious size, the desert is threatening to swallow it up.

pois.name: The House of the Crooked Coin
pois.itName: The House of the Crooked Coin
pois.desc: In a celestial struggle 'twixt Azim and Nhaama, a sliver of her essence was sent tumbling to the earth below. This divine fragment hidden within a mountain cave is said to retain her power, which was harnessed once in the past to avert a terrible calamity.

pois.name: The Hundred-and-one Revelations
pois.desc: As the Uyagir themselves tell it, they live within the cave to make amends for the sins of their forebears, who in their hubris strove to subjugate all creation. As punishment, the gods unleashed a plague of enormous beetles upon them. That their children might never forget, their ancestors moved into the cave, and upon its walls painted murals telling of their misdeeds.

pois.name: The Path of the Craven
pois.desc: This bridge which once extended across the Wound has yet to be restored since it fell into disrepair and collapsed. Before, it served as a simple test for would-be warriors of the Steppe, who must be brave enough to tame and ride a yol. Those who crossed without trouble were deemed worthy, whereas those who hesitated or turned back were found wanting.

pois.name: The Towering Still
pois.desc: The winds of the Steppe break upon these towering cliffs, which extend across the western edge of the region. In truth, the Azim Steppe extends far beyond this mountain range, through few outsiders have journeyed beyond and laid eyes on the lands, much less met the tribes which call them home.

pois.name: The Uyagir Caves
pois.desc: The former home of the Uyagir is said to have been created by the winds of the Steppe, which bored holes into the rock and formed the cave system. At present, a race of oliphant-like beings named Matanga have claimed them as their abode.

pois.name: The Wound
pois.desc: At the base of this deep canyon is one of many rivers which flow into the One River. Xaela legend tells that the great rift was formed long, long ago, before the first Au Ra was created, by the chaos brought about by a terrible battle between the Dawn Father and the Dusk Mother.

pois.name: Bardam's Mettle
pois.desc: Tempra di Bardam: sacro percorso di prova dove i guerrieri della Steppa dimostrano il proprio valore domando lo Yol.

pois.name: Airship Launch
pois.desc: The Crystarium makes scant use of the larger flying vessels, and thus this pier sees little traffic. As relationships with Eulmore continue to improve, however, city officials expect a commensurate surge in aeronave activity.

pois.name: Ballistics
pois.desc: Ballistics is entrusted with developing and storing the weapons and military supplies considered crucial to the city's defense. While the facility originally manufactured more traditional projectile weaponry, they have since shifted production to crystal cannons-magical artillery capable of firing, concentrated etere.

pois.name: Musica Universalis
pois.desc: The largest marketplace in the Crystarium. Though perhaps overly grand in title, Musica Universalis is nevertheless an impressive sight. Its shelves groan under the weight of overwhelming variety, including wares manufactured by the Crystalline Mean and exotic goods imported from locales as distant as Kholusia and Amh Araeng.

pois.name: Spagyrics
pois.desc: More than just a simple infirmary, Spagyrics boasts the facilities for mixing its own medicinal tonics and tinctures, as well as training neophyte chirurgeons. Those familiar with alchemical processes will recognize the name from a procedure for separating and recombining a concoction's primordial elements.

pois.name: Sweetsieve
pois.desc: In contrast to the largely water-based experimental agriculture of the Hortorium, Sweetsieve employs traditional soil and tried-and-true methods to produce abundant fruit. Its trees and vines are lovingly tended in the hopes that the resultant yield is as sweet as the name given to the orchard itself.

pois.name: Syrcus Tower
pois.desc: The soaring centerpiece of the city. The Crystal Tower is home to the Ocular, which serves as the Exarch's office, as well as the Umbilicus, a chamber filled with devices for controlling the spire's functions. It also houses numerous relics of a powerful and dangerous nature, and none are permitted to wander the structure without the Exarch's express permission.

pois.name: Temenos Rookery
pois.desc: Managed almost exclusively by the Zun, this rookery echoes with the sounds of creatures great and small, from the clucks of chickens to the kwehs of chocobos. Said to describe a “sacred enclosure,” the name is a reference to the legendary roosts of the amaro, and indeed, many an amaro is raised from egg to adult within the rookery's well-tended grounds.

pois.name: Tessellation
pois.desc: This grand bridge spans the distance between the Exarch Gate and the Crystarium. It is said that clockwork automata - undoubtedly the product of Allagan technology - marched out from the Crystal Tower to aid in its construction.

pois.name: The Amaro Launch
pois.desc: For the everyday purposes of landing or taking flight, this structure is almost comically large. Its oversized construction, however, was designed to facilitate the deployment of an entire contingent of amaro cavalry in the event that a Lightwarden horde should besiege the city.

pois.name: The Baldaquin
pois.desc: This ever-bustling district contains facilities vital to the continued well-being of the city, such as the Mean's workshops and Spagyrics's infirmary. The plateau neighboring the Mean is given over to the amaro tamers and their charges, with the supports of the Amaro Launch extending out into the surrounding gorge.

pois.name: The Cabinet of Curiosity
pois.desc: This towering vault contains countless scrolls, tomes, and moldering manuscripts salvaged from the furthest reaches of Norvrandt. Representing the grammarian branch of the Trivium, the Cabinet welcomes visitors in search of anything from the most complex academic texts to the illustrated works of children.

pois.name: The Catenaries
pois.desc: A residential quarter for the Crystarium's citizens. It is considered to represent geometric wisdom due to the extremely regular pattern of its construction.

pois.name: The Crystalline Mean
pois.desc: The Crystarium's primary production hub houses a multitude of workshops and storerooms under a single roof. A cacophony of crafting rings out day and night, with the facet-affiliated workers joined by a near-constant influx of independent artisans in search of commissions.

pois.name: The Dossal Gate
pois.desc: The Crystal Tower's sole entrance. In places of worship belonging to the Church of the First Light, the Exedra was uniformly overseen by an alter, thus this gate's metaphorical association with the alterpiece.

pois.name: The Exedra
pois.desc: A broad plaza which one must cross before ascending the steps of the Crystal Tower. As the largest open space in the city, the Exedra is the location of choice for holding festivals, ceremonies, and public addresses.

pois.name: The Gangway
pois.desc: As the name implies, the Gangway is a facility for boarding and disembarking passengers when airships dock in the Crystarium.

pois.name: The Hortorium
pois.desc: Part farm and part research facility, the Hortorium is dedicated to maximizing the yield of aquaculture-grown crops. Deemed the logician's branch of the Trivium, purists would argue that agriculture has little, any, connection to philosophy-the true birthplace of logic. Others contend that naught could be more philosophical than endlessly exploring the means for survival upon a near-desolate star.

pois.name: The Pendants
pois.desc: Built on a similar scale to the Catenaries, this second residential quarter has a suite permanently set aside for the Warrior of Darkness's personal use. It is said that extensive calculations went into providing as much living space as possible for incoming refugees during construction, a process which solidified the Pendants as the perfect embodiment of the field of arithmetic.

pois.name: The Quadrivium
pois.desc: Each of the Quadrivium's divisions is characterized by one of four branches of study-arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, or music. It is these venues wherein the average citizen spends the majority of their time.

pois.name: The Rotunda
pois.desc: Upon stepping foot inside the Crystarium, one is greeted by the sight of a stately domed structure, walkways and hallways branching away from its walls like arteries from a beating heart. Constructed of elegant black iron and sheets of shimmering crystal, it is in the visitor's heart that this building is like to remain.

pois.name: The Trivium
pois.desc: Located in the city's north, the Trivium's constituent parts represent the scholarly branches of grammar, rhetoric, and logic.

pois.name: The Wandering Stairs
pois.desc: The name of the city's sole tavern is also a warning for patrons wont to overindulge: mind your step when you leave. Classifying this establishment as the long-pointless study of astronomy was a nod to the equally meaningless pastime of drinking, which people continue to pursue all the same.

pois.name: The Whispering Gallery
pois.desc: A debate hall for the free and frank exchange of ideas and opinions. In this quite literal incarnation of the branch of rhetoric, many students are eager to share their thoughts on restructuring government policy as the world heads into a new age.

pois.name: The Twinning
pois.desc: Since its sudden appearance in Norvrandt, the Crystal Tower has been a source of great mystery, one which the people of the Crystarium have barely begun to unravel. Now that the city is free from the threat of the Lightwardens, researchers have been afforded the opportunity to explore the innermost reaches of the tower, though they soon found their way barred by hordes of ferocious guardians. An aetherial disturbance detected from inside is believed to be in some way linked to their appearance, and you have been tasked with not only clearing a path for the researchers, but with investigating the cause of the anomaly.

pois.name: Customs Hold
pois.desc: "Do resist the temptation to touch anything in here. The free citizens become quite irate with us if their items have even the slightest hint of a smudge on them when released from customs."

pois.name: Customs Office A-1
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Eulmore.

pois.name: Customs Office A-2
pois.desc: "The list in front of me shows items that the free citizens are interested in obtaining in exchange for goods they no longer want. Have a look if you like.

pois.name: Eulmoran Army Headquarters
pois.desc: The offices of the vaunted Eulmoran military. Though once ensconced in the Canopy above, the change in policy which accompanied Lord Vauthry's investiture as ruler saw the army fall in prominence, its officers relegated to the mid-layer chambers which once served as the city's gaol.

pois.name: Joyous Hall
pois.desc: The entrance hall to Eulmore proper, so named for the elated expressions of successful petitioners. New residents are processed by the Bureaus of Immigration and Registration, before making a stop in the charmingly named Delousery. Outside supplies are also delivered here under the watchful eyes of customs officials.

pois.name: Nightsoil Pots
pois.desc: This modest nursery grows ornamental herbs and flowers to decorate the chambers of free citizens. An unbearable stench arises from the various planters, the sallow earth enriched with rotting food and nightsoil. Still, the compost's effectiveness is undeniable: one would never guess such a desolate world could produce such vibrant blooms.

pois.name: Skyfront
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Eulmore.

pois.name: The Beehive
pois.desc: The Beehive is a place of noise and excitement─a little sting to invigorate the safe, pampered lives of Eulmore's free citizens. Regardless of gender, this establishment's bonded workers are often called “honeybees,” while the owner reigns above them as “queen.”

pois.name: The Bureau of Immigration
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Eulmore.

pois.name: The Bureau of Registration
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Eulmore.

pois.name: The Buttress
pois.desc: If one were to imagine Eulmore as a giant tree, then the Buttress would be its base. And just as a tree's roots draw in water and nutrients, so does the Buttress siphon away the most promising workers to serve as bonded up above. Beneath it is said to be a prison, its cells once used for storage or shelter.

pois.name: The Canopy
pois.desc: The Canopy crowns the top of Eulmore's metaphorical tree, where free citizens enjoy the finer things in life—much as the broadest leaves drink in the most sunlight. An eterite stands in the center of a circular plaza, which is itself ringed by the aerial walkway of Skyfront. The mayor's audience chamber and private quarters, meanwhile, are found on a separate level, above even this lofty platform.

pois.name: The Crown Lift
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Eulmore.

pois.name: The Delousery
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Eulmore.

pois.name: The Glory Gate
pois.desc: This grand entrance leads into the Buttress layer of Eulmore─a sudden and jarring shift into a world of splendor. Crowds of hopeful petitioners yearn for the chance to pass through its ironbound doors, but the path to “glory” is far narrower than the width of the gate would suggest.

pois.name: The Grand Dame's Parlor
pois.desc: This parlor was established by a Voeburtite noblewoman of high status, her exodus credited as a beacon for gathering the wealthy and influential to Eulmore. The current proprietor is one of her descendants, but is said to leave the running of the place to a free citizen who enjoys the idea of working.

pois.name: The Mainstay
pois.desc: This massive pillar provides a core of support for the layers of city above. As it does not connect with the ground, however, the actual weight of upper levels is offset by crystals harvested from a floating island. The overall construction supposedly minimizes the impact of tremors.

pois.name: The Understory
pois.desc: Continuing the arboreal metaphor, the aptly named Understory is Eulmore's trunk. This level has been repurposed for Eulmore's military, and features makeshift barracks and supply closets. The architecture is deliberately fortress-like, allowing a small force to prevent access to the upper layers in the event of an uprising from below.

pois.name: The Xylem Lift
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Eulmore.

pois.name: The Heroes' Gauntlet
pois.desc: La Sfida degli Eroi: campo di battaglia ancestrale dove echi di eroi del passato vengono evocati dallo spettro di Elidibus.

pois.name: Brick
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Lakeland.

pois.name: Clearmelt
pois.desc: The ravages of the Flood saw Clearmelt's once-famous inn repurposed as a treatment facility for the wounded and the weary. Melted snow streaming down from the northern ranges fills its springs with rejuvenating, crystal-clear waters.

pois.name: Dampsole
pois.desc: Proximity to the lake means the ground here is always wet and muddy, a quality which no doubt contributed to the name of this former fishing village. Like many small settlements in Lakeland, it was abandoned after the sin eater host swept through and slaughtered most of its inhabitants.

pois.name: Embrasure
pois.desc: The branching trunk of a giant tree has created this naturally sheltered campsite. Elven patrols would take their rest here, likening the gaps between boles to the openings in a parapet.

pois.name: Fort Jobb
pois.desc: Once the forward base of a long-faded knightly order, these ruins were repurposed to serve as a defensive outpost for the Crystarium guard. The architectural remnants of the Church of the First Light now merely hint at the majesty of a bygone era.

pois.name: Hare Among Giants
pois.desc: The unusual name given to this simple woodcutter's camp was meant to serve as a reminder: here be monsters. While no actual giants were in evidence, workers were encouraged to return home before dark, lest they fall afoul of the forest's savage wildlife.

pois.name: Inviolate Witness
pois.desc: Situated atop a small plateau and connected to Laxan Loft by a stone bridge, this modest arbor once allowed the elven highborn to enjoy the bracing mountain air in peaceful seclusion. Inviolate Witness, as its ruins were later called, has the dubious honor of being the location where a sin eater was first spotted in Lakeland.

pois.name: Knot
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Lakeland.

pois.name: Lap
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Lakeland.

pois.name: Laxan Loft
pois.desc: In the old tongue of the elves, “Laxan” is the word for “Lakeland,” and it is here that the region's erstwhile king set his throne. The castle is also infamous as the site of a historical conflict, where the Shadowkeeper led a force of elven dissidents in a final, bloody uprising.

pois.name: Mortal Irons
pois.desc: Erstwhile home to the wardens of the Hour of Certain Durance, this dwelling was abandoned along with the prison when the region was swarmed with sin eaters, its original name discarded in favor of its present somber title.

pois.name: Northern Staging Point
pois.desc: In the event that the Crystarium guard is required to deploy in force, its soldiers are instructed to muster at this designated site. The staging point saw practical use, for instance, when a rescue company was formed to respond to the attack on Holminster Switch.

pois.name: Radisca's Round
pois.desc: Located in the center of Lakeland, this watchtower is named in honor of a soldier who saved countless lives when he warned of a flying swarm of sin eaters. The soldier himself was slain in battle, having chosen to remain at the tower and delay the eaters' pursuit.

pois.name: Sullen
pois.desc: Weed, Brick, Knot, and Lap─the fishing village of Sullen sprawls across these four small islands, its bridges connecting each location to the next, and thence to the shore of the Source itself. The settlement's name, it seems, was agreed upon as a self-deprecating nod to the oft-creased brows of its resident fishermen.

pois.name: The Accensor Gate
pois.desc: A final checkpoint for travelers before entering the Crystarium, this gate marks the outer edge of the city's territory.

pois.name: The Belt
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Lakeland.

pois.name: The Bridges
pois.desc: Along with Fort Jobb, the Bridges fortify the Crystarium against intrusions by stray eaters or Nightshade, a volatile group of elven traditionalists.

pois.name: The Chiliad
pois.desc: Named by the elves in the distant past, this jagged mountain range enfolding the region of Lakeland was believed to offer the promise of a thousand possibilities.

pois.name: The Church of the First Light
pois.itName: The Church of the First Light
pois.desc: The Church of the First Light was once Lakeland's dominant faith, but the advent of the Flood saw the widespread religion—and its holy places—fall into decline. Historians say that it was barely a decade later when early adopters of Darkness worship began holding their congregations here, in the shell of their predecessor's splendor.

pois.name: The Exarch Gate
pois.desc: The main gate leading into the Crystarium proper, a passage so named not through the Exarch's own choice, but by the repeated usage of all those seeking his succor. From here, travelers set foot on the Belt-a road which cuts across the middle of Lakeland.

pois.name: The Forest of the Lost Shepherd
pois.itName: The Forest of the Lost Shepherd
pois.desc: The lavender foliage of this Lakeland forest is lovely to behold, but even those familiar with its boughs have been known to lose their way. Legend has it that a local shepherd set off into the woods in search of a stray lamb, and never found his way out again.

pois.name: The Hall of the Thrice Born
pois.itName: The Hall of the Thrice Born
pois.desc: Three times has this great hall in Laxan Loft been witness to historical shifts in and three times has a new ruler arisen to take the place of the one before. The third—and perhaps most memorable—occasion was marked by the infamous battle between the Shadowkeeper and the Warriors of Light.

pois.name: The Hanging Tower
pois.desc: A grim tale surrounds this tower which stands within the walls of Laxan Loft: at the sight of the encroaching host of sin eaters, a knight atop the battlements was struck by such profound hopelessness that he took his own life.

pois.name: The Hour of Certain Durance
pois.desc: These crumbling ruins are all that remains of a Lakeland prison. To the east, at the base of the cliff, can be seen another memory of the past─the domiciles of the prison wardens. Once known by a less-somber name, “Mortal Irons” is thought to better reflect the settlement's abandoned state and the transient fate of its residents.

pois.name: The Isle of Ken
pois.desc: Local folklore asserts that a man known as Ken made his home on this small island, and so has the narrative endured. In reality, the isle is an ancient fae being by the name of Bismarck. Bismarck speaks fondly of the man who once dwelt on his back, a mortal unafraid of the preternatural and conversant in the faerie tongue.

pois.name: The Ostall Imperative
pois.desc: The well-preserved remnants of a fortress dating back to the glory days of Lakeland. This imposing structure was named in honor of one Ser Ostall, who, according to the tales, ordered his men to stand their ground against a ravening horde of sin eaters. The knight himself refused to fall, holding off the abominations until the smallfolk had reached safe refuge.

pois.name: The Source
pois.desc: According to elven legend, this majestic lake was the wellspring of all existence on the star. Small wonder, then, that their people have ever expressed a deep reverence for these waters and the lands that surround them.

pois.name: The Stay
pois.desc: This fortification was originally put into place to help secure Laxan Loft against Voeburtite incursions. These days, however, its walls serve as a vantage point from which to keep watch for Il Mheg's more adventurous faeries.

pois.name: The Thirstless Shore
pois.desc: The northern shore of the Source. This edge is perpetually inundated with several ilms of water, its shallows extending inland for some distance.

pois.name: Watts's Anvil
pois.desc: Belonging to an elf by the name of Lorathia, this plot of land was earmarked for use as a Crystalline Mean storehouse. In an unexpected turn of events, however, of young dwarves from Kholusia convinced the irascible owner to lend a group them the spot, which they have since transformed into a factory for manufacturing tanklike conveyances.

pois.name: Weathering
pois.desc: For untold centuries, the wind blowing up from the south has eaten away at this northern rock face. Once the natural border with the neighboring Kingdom of Voeburt, it would have been heavily patrolled by Lakeland's forces.

pois.name: Weed
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Lakeland.

pois.name: Wolves of Shadow
pois.desc: This ruined mansion was once home to a high-ranking elven noble-a man who had pledged fealty to the Shadowkeeper in the hopes of restoring his people's supremacy. In return for his allegiance, he and his entire family were transformed into lupine soldiers, and to this day do they wander the land as fell beasts.

pois.name: Holminster Switch
pois.desc: Holminster Switch─an idyllic settlement in the northern reaches of Lakeland; a tranquil village where folk spend their days raising livestock and tending crops; a ripe target for a Lightwarden and its swarm of voracious sin eaters. Reports of bloody carnage have reached the Crystarium, and the guard has deployed in force in answer to Holminster's plea for aid. The Crystal Exarch has need of your strength, for this is no skirmish with a stray abomination─to triumph against a Warden would be to strike a telling blow in the unending war for the First's survival.

pois.name: The Grand Cosmos
pois.desc: Long ago, on the far shore of the Source, a great palace was built by the elves─the Grand Cosmos, an edifice of such magnitude it was said to inspire envy in both the heavens for which it was named and the flowers that pervade its boundless gardens. As with so many wonders of the world that once was, its radiance quickly faded in the wake of the Flood, its halls falling silent, the throne sitting empty. That is, until the palace was given new purpose when a mage claimed it as their sanctuary, their only company being solace, solitude, and the legion of familiars barring entrance to any foolish enough to seek an audience.

pois.name: Amity
pois.desc: A thriving center for trade with the dwarves, Amity's importance evaporated under Lord Vauthry's restrictive policies. Its faded status has since made it the perfect hideaway for fugitives fleeing the cruel vagaries of Eulmore.

pois.name: Barrow Isle
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: Boiled Owl Bridge
pois.desc: Flowing from its source in the Duergar Mountains, the upper stretch of Watts River is spanned at two spots by the Flue and Boiled Owl Bridges. Crossing over to the river's east side puts one squarely in Gogg territory.

pois.name: Bottom Rung
pois.desc: This facility oversaw the operation of the Ladder and served as a hub for the transport of trade goods. In earlier days, ore purchased from the highland dwarves would be packed here, ready for shipment to Eulmore, but Lord Vauthry's despotic rule saw the Bottom Rung fall into disuse.

pois.name: Cracked Shell Beach
pois.desc: When questioned on the rather prosaic name of this coastline, the inhabitants of nearby Stilltide simply point to the carpet of broken seashells. In earlier days, they say the beach was crowded with the comings and goings of local fishermen, but now it is mostly the boots of barbaric hobgoblins leaving tracks along the pebbled shore.

pois.name: Dwarven Hollows
pois.desc: Bitter rivals in all things but especially excavation, both Tholl and Gogg lay claim to this cavernous network of mining tunnels. Outsiders simply refer to them as the Dwarven Hollows in a conscious attempt to avoid antagonizing either tribe.

pois.name: Flue Bridge
pois.desc: Flowing from its source in the Duergar Mountains, the upper stretch of Watts River is spanned at two spots by the Flue and Bowled Oil Bridges. Crossing over to the river's east side puts one squarely in Gogg territory.

pois.name: Gatetown
pois.desc: Gatetown is a haphazard mess of shacks and lean-tos─the result of refugees throwing up shelters as they await their chance to embrace the comforts of Eulmore. Though living conditions can best be described as “abysmal,” the regular distribution of meol and minimal risk of eater attacks has only seen the population increase over time.

pois.name: Governor's Row
pois.desc: It is said that Stilltide's mayor took to calling himself "governor" to intimidate Eulmoran officials. The farming plot which shares his grandiose title was given over to the care of a local villager, who has since been lured away by the stories of meol and an easier life.

pois.name: Greely Bridge
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: Greely Sties
pois.desc: This pig farm was abandoned after a pack of wild animals butchered the entire sty. The Greelys' daughter sought a new life in Wright, but tragedy struck again when her betrothed was slain by a stray eater. Locals say she was driven mad with grief and drowned herself in the nearby river.

pois.name: Komra
pois.desc: Another of the dwarven settlements found on the slopes of Mt. Gulg, Komra is home to a proud branch of the Gogg family. The village was nearly obliterated by otherworldly forces, but the resilient residents have pulled together to rebuild their lives (and their houses).

pois.name: Longbeard Council
pois.desc: The Tholl elders gather here to debate matters of import. Judging by the sounds of revelry which often echo within, no matter is more important than imbibing copious quantities of Tholl-brewed ale.

pois.name: Open Arms
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: Pit 8
pois.desc: The dwarves of Tomra built this secret tunnel for Amity's reclusive residents. Disguised as a mining camp, its extensive shafts allow one to bypass the Ladder completely when traveling between highlands and lowlands.

pois.name: Scree
pois.desc: Encompassing the lower slopes of Mt. Gulg, this jagged landscape is rich with ore deposits. The highlands of Scree are known as the ancestral home of the dwarves, and the Tholl in particular have a strong presence in the region.

pois.name: Seagazer
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: Shadow Fault
pois.desc: Even on the brightest day, the glowering cliffs cast long shadows over this stretch of the island. A number of towers keep watch over the dreary landscape, with Stonegazer on guard for bandits and dwarves from the highlands, and Seagazer scanning the ocean for approaching pirates.

pois.name: Sharptongue Drip
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: Slowroad
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: Southern Crossing
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: Stilltide
pois.desc: The people of this modest fishing village subsist on sea life, reeling in catches from what little of the ocean remains free from Light's stasis. Even here, however, the effects of the Flood have turned the waters' current slow and sluggish.

pois.name: Stonegazer
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: The Bright Cliff
pois.desc: This section of sheer cliff and the lands at its base are situated such that they bathe in sunlight for the greater part of the day. Bestowed in the distant past, the locale's name gained a touch of irony during the perpetual illumination brought about by the Flood.

pois.name: The Chisel
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: The Clave
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: The Codger's Crook
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: The Duergar Mountains
pois.desc: This series of foreboding peaks form Kholusia's northeastern mountain range. The very fact that the ancient word for "dwarf" was used to name the mountains indicates just how long the short-statured race has dwelled here.

pois.name: The Duergar's Tewel
pois.desc: The far end of the Dwarven Hollows opens up into a great, crater-like expanse. Geysers here spew volcanically heated water high into the air, spraying the uncaring dwarves as they mine deposits of sulphur and other valuable minerals.

pois.name: The Ladder
pois.desc: This enormous mechanism facilitates travel between Kholusia's lowlands and highlands. Its gears once driven by the tireless Talos of Daedalus Stoneworks, the apparatus fell into disrepair after said company retired its operations in the region─a development which all but halted trade with the highland dwarves.

pois.name: The Leaky Keel
pois.desc: Stilltide's one and only tavern offers the locals a place to gather and guzzle down bottles of the proprietress's home-brewed mead. Theva runs her place with a sharp tongue, but is known to fuss over her fellow villagers like an overbearing mother hen.

pois.name: The Split Hull
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: The Wet Whistle
pois.desc: The village drinkers gather here to imbibe copious amounts of Gogg-brewed ale. On rare occasions, the raised voices actually belong to the chief and the elders as they consult on matters of import.

pois.name: The Whale's Breach
pois.desc: This promontory leading into Eulmore is said to vaguely resemble the shape of a whale heaved up onto the beach. Once marked only by the paved path of Slowroad, the locale has long since become cluttered with makeshift hovels

pois.name: Tomra
pois.desc: One of the dwarven settlements which dot the slopes of Mt. Gulg, Tomra is home to a sizable branch of the Tholl family. Every building is constructed on a scale to cater to the diminutive inhabitants, giving taller races the impression of a village built in miniature.

pois.name: Top Rung
pois.desc: As the name implies, this counterpart facility to the Bottom Rung stands at the Ladder's apex. In its glory days, the complex was filled with trundling Talos, shifting and stacking boxes of cargo.

pois.name: Venmont Yards
pois.desc: Bearing the name of a famous shipwright, these shipyards were once a pillar of Eulmore's commercial industry. With the loss of the oceans to the Light, however, there is little demand for seafaring vessels, and the builders' descendants have thus turned their woodworking skills to crafting homes and furniture.

pois.name: Wax Seal Mills
pois.desc: This site was once home to a crowded sheep pasture, the air thick with the cries of ovine contentment. Now only the windmills used to full their wool remain, a pair of somber sentinels without a flock to tend.

pois.name: Whisperwind Cove
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Kholusia.

pois.name: White Oil Falls
pois.desc: This waterfall marks the midpoint of Watts River. The sluggish current sends water over the cliff with little force, the cascade cleaving closely to the rock as it plunges down from an impressive height. Upon observing this almost-viscous flow, a renowned poet is said to have likened the falls to an enormous trickle of oil.

pois.name: Wright
pois.desc: A farming village in the southern reaches of Kholusia. The residents of Wright have refused the largesse of Eulmore, preferring instead to subsist upon barley, vegetables, and other crops cultivated through time-honored methods. Their independence cost them dearly, however, when the appearance of a stray sin eater ended in unspeakable slaughter.

pois.name: Mt. Gulg
pois.desc: Toppled from his seat of power, Vauthry, the final Lightwarden, has fled to Mt. Gulg, whose fiery summit now hangs in the firmament, beyond his enemies' reach. However, with the aid of the myriad peoples of Norvrandt, you succeed in building a gigantic Talos that rises to take the volcano in its grasp. Using the golem's rocky body as a bridge, you begin the arduous ascent to your quarry's newly built paradise, there to put an end to the tyranny of Light.

pois.name: Anamnesis Anyder
pois.desc: Deep in the Tempest─deeper still than the phantom Amaurot of Emet-Selch's design─lies what remains of Anyder's ancient edifices. It is to an unexplored corner of this bed of knowledge that the Scions now travel, in hopes that what has long slumbered forgotten may be brought to the surface once more.

pois.name: Garik
pois.desc: Though it was once a bustling mining town, Garik's inhabitants evacuated en masse to escape the approaching Flood. Mord merchants later moved into the abandoned cabins, only too happy to claim such a convenient trading post for doing business with their Lakeland partners.

pois.name: Kelk
pois.desc: The ruins of a Ronso settlement. Residents abandoned Kelk for the cities long before the Flood arrived, and thus it is known amongst scavengers as a prime location for finding trinkets and relics untouched by conflict.

pois.name: Ladle
pois.desc: This now-dilapidated station for Talos-drawn trolleys served the needs of passengers traveling to and from the city. Shipments of water drawn from Malikah's Well were also loaded here for transport.

pois.name: Lift Station
pois.desc: Scavengers built this pulley-and-rope mechanism to facilitate the recovery of precious artifacts from the ruins of Nabaath Areng. As the city has since been picked clean of treasures, however, the winch's condition has deteriorated from disuse.

pois.name: Mord Souq
pois.desc: The Mord have long dwelled in Amh Araeng, and this “souq” or “city” serves as a marketplace to display the curious wares they gather from every corner of the badlands. Merchants and collectors from across Norvrandt can be seen here purchasing ores, oddities, and the relics of Nabaath Areng.

pois.name: Mount Biran Mines
pois.desc: The shafts carved into the side of Mount Biran were the center of a large-scale mining operation which employed the relentless strength of an army of Talos. As is the case with Garik, Kelk, and many other places in the region, “Biran” was a name taken from a Ronso of historical note.

pois.name: Nabaath Areng
pois.desc: An oasis of desert commerce, the Nabaath Empire's capital built its wealth on the trade of local minerals, both precious and mundane. The civilization now lies broken, the gargantuan wave of frozen Light yet looming in its midst. Flakes of crystallized radiance have fallen away from the main mass, each smaller shard a source of glittering peril.

pois.name: Nuvy's Leavings
pois.desc: The history of this mine stretches back to the time of the Ronkan Empire. Ronso workers labored to carve out its winding shafts, but there was a limit to how deep they could dig with only pickaxes and persistence. The Nabaath Empire commissioned a project to reopen the excavation using Talos, but as with many endeavors of that age, the scheme fell by the wayside with the advent of the Flood.

pois.name: Our Ladies' Feet
pois.desc: Another contraption built by the Mord, this windmill is used for crushing the wildly diverse ingredients mixed into the local brews. Similar to the Ladies' Hands, the technology replaces a process that once involved a great deal of jumping and stomping.

pois.name: Our Ladies' Hands
pois.desc: Built high up to catch the wind whistling through the mountains, this windmill is put to steady use by the Mord to grind popoto-like desert tubers into flour. Its name is an expression of gratitude, the technology replacing what was once a laborious task carried out by hand.

pois.name: Pitch
pois.desc: One of several watchtowers constructed to guard against bandits preying on Mord trade routes. Its sister spires are known as Snitch and Twitch.

pois.name: Qasr Sharl
pois.desc: Literally translated, Qasr Sharl means "Castle North" in the old tongue of Nabaath Areng. This now-tilted fortification stands guard on the nation's northern border, the hulking ruins empty but for the sand and a handful of enterprising merchants

pois.name: Samiel's Backbone
pois.desc: According to Mord mythology, these bones belonged to a colossal creature known as a samiel. Many believe its ghost still roams the sands, and young Mord are known to dare each other to spend the night beneath its fossilized remains.

pois.name: Snitch
pois.desc: One of several watchtowers constructed to guard against bandits preying on Mord trade routes. Its sister spires are known as Snitch and Twitch.

pois.name: The Central Hills of Amber
pois.desc: The central hills of Amh Araeng were the heart of Nabaath Areng's mining industry, with trolley tracks cutting north and south through the countryside. One band of young entrepreneurs is determined to repair the railway and return the mining operations to their former glory.

pois.name: The Derrick
pois.desc: This basic wooden outpost was erected to keep watch for winged sin eaters flying into the desert from the Empty. Guard rosters are presently managed by the Inn at Journey's Head.

pois.name: The Dragging Tail
pois.desc: Likened to the long, curved tail of a Mord, this tunnel is a repurposed mineshaft which provides a direct passage from Mord Souq to the central hills.

pois.name: The Fields of Amber
pois.desc: In the days before the Flood, caravans of heavily laden amaro could be seen wending their way across the amber desert. Merchants of the present age yet follow the same routes to market, though they are a far less common sight than they once were.

pois.name: The Inn at Journey's Head
pois.desc: This facility was established as an infirmary for treating victims of eater metamorphosis, though failure to find a viable cure swiftly dashed any initial optimism. It then became the Inn at Journey's Head—a place for sufferers to live out their last days in peaceful seclusion. Recent breakthroughs, however, have been successful in reversing the condition, and what was an air of grim surrender is now one of quiet hope.

pois.name: The Nabaath Severance
pois.desc: This sheer drop was formed in the wake of the Flood. The name is both literal and metaphorical, representative of the physical changes to the landscape as well as the abrupt end which befell the Nabaath Empire.

pois.name: The Northern Hills of Amber
pois.desc: In contrast to the transient sands of the Fields of Amber, the highland plateaus of northwestern Amh Araeng sit atop a stable foundation of rock. A clan of Ronso relocated here during the reign of the Ronkan Empire, leaving their mark-and their names-on the region's mine sand settlements.

pois.name: The Pristine Palace of Amh Malik
pois.itName: The Pristine Palace of Amh Malik
pois.desc: In the common tongue, “amh malik” translates into “majestic king,” and it was within this royal residence that was housed the core of Nabaath Areng's political and military might. When the Flood came, however, it was halted moments too late─half the palace toppled before a titanic wave of Light like a sand castle caught by the tide.

pois.name: The Rack
pois.desc: This stone tower is easily the tallest structure in Mord Souq. Its spacious interior is used to store all manner of valuable inventory, and as such, entry to the Rack is denied to market patrons.

pois.name: The Red Serai
pois.desc: This amaro roost was established by Crystarium merchants plying their trade in Amh Araeng. Tucked within the foreboding walls of Qasr Sharl, the waypoint and its stockpiled goods are well protected from both predators and windblown sands.

pois.name: The Southern Hills of Amber
pois.desc: The southern hills are known as the location of Malikah's Well. This famous landmark was built in remembrance of one of the ancient kings of Nabaath Areng, its subterranean waters once providing a welcome source of respite from the desert heat.

pois.name: Twine
pois.desc: In days past, Nabaath Areng contracted a Talos engineer to establish its mining railway, and these cabins were built to provide lodgings for the laborers who would lay the trolley tracks. The settlement was later maintained as a miners' village, but its dwindling population has mirrored the steady decline of the mining industry.

pois.name: Twitch
pois.desc: One of several watchtowers constructed to guard against bandits preying on Mord trade routes. Its sister spires are known as Snitch and Twitch.

pois.name: Malikah's Well
pois.desc: Pozzo di Malikah: imponente opera idraulica dei nani sepolta sotto le sabbie dorate del Nabaath Areng.

pois.name: Anden's Airs
pois.desc: Unwilling to abandon his home even in the face of an eater invasion, the shepherd Anden spent his last days as a mortal man among his flock. When the pixies learned of his refusal to flee, they transformed him into a leafman that he might watch over his "sweet fluffies" for eternity.

pois.name: Deepwood Swim
pois.desc: In the time of Voeburt, when Lyhe Ghiah was yet known as Gruenes Licht, these ruins were a thriving castle town. Now they languish at the bottom of Longmirror Lake, submerged in the waters drawn forth by the Fuath as the faeries laid claim to Il Mheg.

pois.name: Father Collard's Chambers
pois.desc: With the aid of his Nu Mou assistant, the eponymous monk cultivated mush- rooms in this secluded cavern as part of his research into apothecary. The lawless ones coveted the cultivars for their potent effects, and so seized the chance afforded by the Flood to usurp control of the chambers and their fantastical fungi.

pois.name: Good Jenanna's Grace
pois.desc: Her Royal Highness Princess Jenanna was daughter to a Voeburtite king of generations past. In the dark of night, this mountain pass catches the light which shines forth from Lyhe Ghiah, the jade glow reminiscent of the princess's beautiful eyes.

pois.name: Handmirror Lake
pois.desc: This lake on the western edge of Il Mheg was once the site of a royal picnic, or so the tale goes. A Voeburtite princess spent the day here with a gaggle of lords and ladies, partaking of tea and sweets and quite ruining her lip paint. She inspected her reflection, as if the tranquil waters were her personal mirror, and the lake has been known thusly ever since.

pois.name: Longmirror Lake
pois.desc: A creation of the faeries, this vast body of water dwarfs Handmirror Lake in size, and so does its name reflect its expansive shape. Beneath its crystal-clear surface can be seen the remnants of the preceding mortal kingdom.

pois.name: Lydha Lran
pois.desc: Finding it abandoned by its former inhabitants following the events of the Flood, the pixies have claimed this Voeburtite village as their own. The fae have continued the villagers' practice of keeping sheep, making use of the weed-choked pens to raise and milk their wooly livestock.

pois.name: Lyhe Ghiah
pois.desc: Once the royal seat of Voeburt, Lyhe Ghiah later became a prison for Titania when the faerie king succumbed to the etere of a slain Lightwarden. The castle's name has its origin in both the faerie and Voeburtite tongues, the words thought to translate as the “wings of dreams.”

pois.name: Mithai Glorianda
pois.desc: Once the heartland of the Kingdom of Voeburt, the castle and its surrounds have long since been claimed as the domain of the faerie king. In the fae tongue, "Mithai" means "mother," and the "Glorianda” it prefaces was known as the legendary Forebear of Pixies.

pois.name: Old Earra Bridge
pois.desc: To visit Gruenes Licht on foot entailed an exhausting climb up this series of elegant yet punishingly steep stairs. Inevitably, perhaps, there was also said to be a service offering amaro-back flights to the castle's forecourt.

pois.name: Phisor Lran
pois.desc: The retinue of trees surrounding this domicile-formerly a shepherd's abode- attracted the pixies' attention. One particularly curious faerie wondered what fruits or nuts the boughs might be hiding, but never returned from their gathering. It was around that same time that an odd beaver-like creature was spotted waddling about the premises.

pois.name: Pla Enni
pois.desc: Known for their harmonious relationship with the now-faded Kingdom of Voeburt, the Nu Mou people reside in this cavern under the leadership of their elder, Wyd Aenc. As well as being the name of the village, “pla enni” is a variety of mushroom the Nu Mou grow to incredible size─large enough for them to hollow out and use as comfortable dwellings.

pois.name: Saint Fathric's Temple
pois.desc: This secluded mountain shelf was favored by Saint Fathric of the Church of the First Light as a place to perform rites of penance. Amongst the faeries of Il Mheg, only the Nu Mou would remember or understand the significance of the location's history.

pois.name: Sextuplet Shallow
pois.desc: These shallows are fed by streams flowing from half a dozen mountain waterfalls. One of the more macabre legends claims that the pixies sacrificed six infant siblings, interring their souls in the rock to conjure this bountiful source of water.

pois.name: The Bookman's Shelves
pois.desc: Lately the borrowed residence of a foreign scholar, this manor once belonged to a Voeburtite lord known for the eclectic nature of his hobbies. In a miraculous turn of events, the noble's extensive collection of books and academic apparatus have largely been left undisturbed by curious pixie hands.

pois.name: The Church at Dammroen Field
pois.desc: In the early days of Voeburt's founding, a shepherd was scouring the woods in search of stray sheep. What she stumbled across instead was a long-forgotten church of the First Light, and a weeping statue of its radiant deity. The tales of pilgrims journeying from afar to marvel at her discovery are many and well documented, yet if one is to visit the ruins today, the miraculous sculpture in question is nowhere to be found.

pois.name: The House of the First Light
pois.itName: The House of the First Light
pois.desc: The tallest spire of this sunken house of worship yet peeks above the surface of the lake. All the lands of Norvrandt echoed with prayers to the Light, and Voeburt was no different—churches large and small graced every corner of the kingdom, from the richest town to the meanest mountain hamlet.

pois.name: The March of the Marchioness
pois.desc: The giant tree near the water's edge of Dohn Mheg is referred to as the marchioness. The pixies tell the story of a fierce Voeburtite general who fought against the eaters till the bitter end-and how they "gifted" her with a floral form as grand and beautiful as her spirit.

pois.name: The Silent Cliffs
pois.desc: After fleeing to the clifftops to escape the eaters, the townspeople were struck dumb when they turned to behold the transformation wrought upon their home. It is thought that most never again had the chance to speak before the faeries came and changed them all into mute leafmen.

pois.name: The Woolen Way
pois.desc: Nu Mou legend has it that in the days when mortals lived in these parts, great wagons went up and down the Woolen Way, each packed to the brim with the fluffiest of fleeces to be carried to market. These days─alas!─only the name remains. Is that not the saddest story you've ever heard? But no matter, for we shall spin a new Woolen Way in the dreams of the children─and one even more glorious than ever before!

pois.name: Thysm Lran
pois.desc: The current residents have dubbed this watery abode "our stately mansion." Once a part of the Kingdom of Voeburt, it now belongs unequivocally to the Fuath.

pois.name: Timh Gyeus
pois.desc: The lush fields and rolling hills in the southwest of Il Mheg were once home to mortal shepherds and their flocks of well-tended sheep. Roughly translated, the faeries' name for this region means "our rose-colored bed."

pois.name: Voeburtenburg
pois.desc: This corner of the former Kingdom of Voeburt is inhabited by the Nu Mou, a fae race which maintained favorable relations with the mortals of that now-fallen nation. In stark contrast to the pixies, the Nu Mou have retained the original Voeburtite names for many of the locales and landmarks.

pois.name: Wolekdorf
pois.desc: Amaro who have awoken to the old blood have gathered in these ruins to form a communal sanctuary. The settlement itself was built before the founding of Voeburt, and is believed to have been a monastery affiliated with the Church at Dammroen Field.

pois.name: Dohn Mheg
pois.desc: Your quest to gain entry to Lyhe Ghiah and vanquish the Lightwarden sealed within has brought you to the domain of the water-bound Fuath, bearers of one of the four fae relics that comprise the key to the castle. The creatures agree to yield to you their relic, the shell crown, but in exchange they demand of you what they call “thrilling sport.” In order to fulfill your side of the bargain, you and your comrades sally forth into a realm of illusion as treacherous and unpredictable as its denizens...

pois.name: Bowrest
pois.desc: Lying some distance outside of Fanow, this camp has become a permanent fixture for the hunters who patrol the woods. Some prefer to sleep here rather than the village, often camping out in the wild for months at a time.

pois.name: Cleric
pois.desc: The Night's Blessed built this rudimentary cabin in the roots of a giant tree as a place to rest while hunting or gathering in the wood. It also serves as a forward post, where scouts can keep an eye on the comings and goings of a rival faction of Dark worshipers known as the Children of the Everlasting Dark.

pois.name: Fanow
pois.desc: Unfailingly loyal to the last-known commands of the Ronkan emperor, the Viis of this village have protected the ruins of Rak'tika for countless generations. With many of its sister settlements destroyed by the Flood of Light, however, Fanow faces an uncertain fate in its isolation.

pois.name: Fort Gohn
pois.desc: Built by the Night's Blessed, little now remains of this wooden fortification. By all accounts, a fire broke out during a sin eater attack, and even before the violence had ended, the compound had collapsed into a charred ruin. Survivors of the slaughter had had no choice but to relocate to the nearby Slitherbough.

pois.name: Fruit of the Protector
pois.desc: Cradled within the branches of a giant tree, this immense crystal boulder is suspended above the waters of Lake Tusi Mek'ta. The “Fruit of the Protector,” as it is known, has been the subject of worship since the time of the Ronkan Empire, and even now folk tell the legend of the great entity believed to be cocooned within.

pois.name: Hopl's Stopple
pois.desc: The entrance here leads to a subterranean network supposedly constructed by the Qitari in the twilight years of the Ronkan Empire. Tunnels sprawl below like a great web, serving as the secret archives for stelae their people engraved with the grand history of Ronka.

pois.name: Lake Tusi Mek'ta
pois.desc: Ruins of ancient Ronka slumber unseen on the bed of this murky lake. The origin of "Tusi Mek'ta" is similarly unclear-some say the old Ronkan words refer to a watery lair where the great serpent of legend manifests its majesty, while others claim it is simply a poetic rendering of the tree roots that snake out over the water's surface.

pois.name: Lozatl's Conquest
pois.desc: According to Ronkan legend, the great steps of this waterfall were carved by the giant Lozatl. Historians speculate that this mythical figure was, in fact, an early form of Talos, and likely the selfsame construct responsible for building Ronka's resplendent places of worship.

pois.name: Mjrl's Regret
pois.desc: Tales tell of a heartbroken Viis who, for reasons unknown, chose to leave her village behind. Standing before the caves and full of sorrow for her lost home, the tears she shed became the river which now crosses the woods from Lozatl's Conquest to this lonely drop downstream.

pois.name: Ox'Charl Mul
pois.desc: The pyramid dedicated to Ox'Charl, keeper of the winds, god of music and the moon. Represents the star of wind.

pois.name: Ox'Gatorl Mul
pois.desc: The pyramid dedicated to Ox'Gatorl, keeper of the flame, god of war and the sun. Represents the star of fire.

pois.name: Sleepaway Common
pois.desc: A communal rest area. Villagers would remark that the everlasting Light shining through the gaps in the canopy above made for comforting naps, as it helped them to imagine real sunlight. Now that sunlight has returned, villagers remark that the blowing breeze makes for comforting naps. It may, in fact, simply be a comfortable place for villagers to nap.

pois.name: Slitherbough
pois.desc: The Night's Blessed reside here under the religious guidance of their priests, bound by their shared faith in the Dark. The branches arching over the settlement cast long shadows on the ground, the patterns reminiscent of a coiling serpent.

pois.name: The Blind Forest of Yx'Maja
pois.desc: Encompassing the eastern reaches of the Greatwood, this band of forest is named for Yx'Maja, the Ronkan goddess of beauty and the hunt. It is believed that she taught the Viis their hunting skills, and their people have thus protected her sacred lands since time immemorial.

pois.name: The Citia Swamps
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a The Rak'tika Greatwood.

pois.name: The Confessional of Toupasa the Elder
pois.itName: The Confessional of Toupasa the Elder
pois.desc: The private chapel of Toupasa the Elder, a hero of legendary status even amongst the ranks of the Ronkan Empire's greatest rulers. The ruins' source of power is said to lie even deeper within.

pois.name: The Covered Halls of Dwatl
pois.desc: One of the sacred temples built by the Ronkans, these stone halls were safeguarded by a sect of priests even after the fall of the empire. The rising waters of the lake, however, could not be denied, and rumors persist of a secret treasure which was swallowed along with the temple.

pois.name: The Darker
pois.desc: This place of worship has been set up inside a natural cavern, the location chosen to prevent exposure to the merest hint of everlasting Light. The faithful come here to meditate, as well as hold funeral rites for the departed.

pois.name: The Deliberating Doll
pois.desc: One legend claims that this squat mountain resting by the shore of Lake Tusi Mek'ta is actually a Ronkan guardian, its duty at an end after battling the entity now sealed within Fruit of the Protector. A different legend disputes this tale, insisting that the battle was fought by Lozatl, a giant whose name yet graces the nearby waterfall.

pois.name: The Great Pyramid of Ux'ner
pois.desc: Though still an impressive structure, the largest of the pyramids has lost some of its majesty to a gigantic tree root crushing it from above. The end of the root has pierced through to a lower level, breaking open a wall and creating an opening into the ruins.

pois.name: The Husk
pois.desc: Although nestled in a tree's embrace like the Fruit of the Protector, this dull hunk of crystal appears devoid of etere. Such lack of perceptible life energy has led some to assert that whatever divine being may have dwelled within, it has long since left—or perished.

pois.name: The Isle of Bows
pois.desc: One of several earthen platforms suspended over the Ox'Dalan Gap, this island is oft visited by Fanow youths as part of their rite of passage. The rite demands they craft a bow of their own, and the sacred trees here provide the needed materials.

pois.name: The Isle of Consorts
pois.desc: It is said that male Viis sneak onto this isle before approaching Fanow in search of a seasonal mate, with a warning hail of arrows meeting any suitor unlucky enough to be spotted. The ability to remain undetected until the courtship of a chosen partner has begun is thus considered the mark of an accomplished hunter.

pois.name: The Isle of Sisters
pois.desc: A pair of Viis sisters would often come here to escape their chores in the village. Viis are, however, possessed of incredibly sharp hearing, and the siblings' muffled voices could still be heard from the other side of Fanow.

pois.name: The K'mul Astropolis
pois.desc: Pyramids honoring the Ronkan gods dominate the astropolis, the surrounding ruins crowded with stone monuments and animated guardians. The energies emanating from the Great Pyramid of Ux'ner suffuse the remnants, lighting every surface with a pale orange glow.

pois.name: The Morning Stars
pois.desc: These pyramids were built to venerate the four chief deities of the Ronkan religion: Ox'Gatorl, keeper of flame; Ox'Charl, keeper of the winds; Yx'Lokwa, bringer of rain; and Yx'Anpa, bringer of the harvest. For the inhabitants of Fanow, guardians of Ronka's heritage, there are few sites more sacred.

pois.name: The Ox'Dalan Gap
pois.desc: This yawning chasm splits the Blind Forest in half. Running east to west, any attempts to guess at its depth are defeated by obscuring gloom, so it is perhaps natural, then, that it bears the name of Ox'Dalan—Ronkan god of the underworld.

pois.name: The Red Chalice
pois.desc: The Children of the Everlasting Dark believe the waters of Lake Tusi Mek'ta to be tainted by perpetual Light. According to their faith, the Red Chalice lies protected under the canopy of the woods, and thus its blessed liquid is safe to imbibe. In practice, however, their properties are essentially identical.

pois.name: The Trip
pois.desc: The protruding roots of these towering swamp trees create a strange and unsettling landscape. Various vilekin and wild birds make their nests in these tangled shelters, contributing to the area's unique ecosystem.

pois.name: The Wild Fete
pois.desc: In a corner of the forest to the east of Slitherbough can be seen a path of brilliant blue flowers. Believed to be the footfalls of the goddess as she stalked her prey through the woods, the Viis call these floral trails the Steps of Maja.

pois.name: The Womb
pois.desc: Hidden deep within the passages of Woven Oath is a humble altar to the Dark. The Children, it is said, were "born" here, guided by the wisdom of Austadia, their founding leader.

pois.name: Woven Oath
pois.desc: This network of caves is home to the Children of the Everlasting Dark-a faction which splintered from the Night's Blessed. Within its twisting tunnels can be found historical artifacts-ancient murals among other things-including a monument inscribed with Ronkan text and its corresponding translation.

pois.name: Yx'Anpa Mul
pois.desc: The pyramid dedicated to Yx'Anpa, bringer of the harvest, goddess of crops and the soil. Represents the star of earth.

pois.name: Yx'Lokwa Mul
pois.desc: The pyramid dedicated to Yx'Lokwa, bringer of rain, goddess of groundwater and solace. Represents the star of water.

pois.name: The Qitana Ravel
pois.desc: The empire of Ronka was a place of magic and enlightenment, of peace and prosperity. Sadly, it was not meant to last. Though naught but ruins remain, they remain heavily guarded nonetheless. The Qitana Ravel is perhaps the most sacred of these sites, home to the ancient wisdom of the past. With the advent of the Flood, however, you have reason to believe something more sinister now resides there as well.

pois.name: Achora Heights
pois.desc: The lift inside this structure carries passengers between its top floor and the ground below. The party of the Warrior of Darkness used this mechanism to enter Amaurot when they first came upon Emet-Selch's phantom creation.

pois.name: Amaurot
pois.desc: If Ondo testimony is to be believed, this vast city simply appeared overnight. Unlike the ancient remnants which endure silently upon the sea floor, its illuminated towers are of a decidedly different nature─a meticulously new and vibrant metropolis, compelling in its mystery.

pois.name: Bureau of the Administrator
pois.desc: Records for every resident of the star were kept in this institution. Its clerks were also responsible for authorizing visitors to the city's august Capitol.

pois.name: Bureau of the Architect
pois.desc: This bureau was responsible for the registration and archiving of concepts, the specific instructions needed to manifest a certain object or entity using creation magicks. Registered concepts could also be borrowed by others upon submission of a successful application.

pois.name: Bureau of the Secretariat
pois.desc: All manner of official documentation and applications were managed by this office, including the issuance of visitor's writs. It seems that even a grand civilization capable of godlike creation sorceries was unable to free itself from the nightmare of labyrinthine bureaucracy.

pois.name: Purpure
pois.desc: The Ondo use the shells they gather from this cave to make dye, the purple hue prized as a symbol of nobility. It is said that Eulmore's obsession with the color purple can be traced back to these underwater origins.

pois.name: The Caliban Gap
pois.desc: The fish god Caliban is thought to have made its lair here, but no sign of the divine wavekin remains. Intruders are wise to be cautious, however, for there are always other predators in the sea.

pois.name: The Caliban Gorge
pois.desc: This ocean chasm is spoken of as the domain of Caliban, a great fish god of legend. The gorge's confusing topography is difficult to navigate, even for the Ondo, but those venturing deep are rewarded with the sight of sunken ships.

pois.name: The Capitol
pois.desc: This stately building was the meeting place of the Convocation of Fourteen, the ultimate authority whose policies dictated the fate of the star. The debate over how the ancients would overcome the Final Days was held within these very walls.

pois.name: The Crock of Pearls
pois.desc: The hefty pearls harvested from the giant mollusks of this spawning grounds are of immense value—fit for the jewelry of an Ondo queen.

pois.name: The Flounders' Floor
pois.desc: An antagonistic tribe of Ondo known as the benthos have claimed these caverns as their home. They wish no dealings with the surface dwellers no matter the circumstance, likening themselves to those sea creatures which cleave to the ocean floor.

pois.name: The Hall of Rhetoric
