pois.desc: The ancients used this hall for formal debates and discussion, their practically immortal lifespans allowing endless hours to enjoy the exploration of ideas and dissenting opinions. Especially insightful rhetoric was recorded and stored in the building's archives.

pois.name: The Macarenses Angle
pois.desc: A simple eterite plaza, the name of which essentially translates as "the land of happiness.” In the days of old, Amaurotines would meet visiting or returning colleagues here, and it was common to see groups lingering in the square, engaged in lively debates.

pois.name: The Norvrandt Slope
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a The Tempest.

pois.name: The Ondo Cups
pois.desc: Hidden at the bottom of the Tempest, this Ondo settlement was established by those few foragers who escaped the Flood's destruction of their homeland. The “Cups” has its origin in the hollows on the shore which remain filled with seawater when the tide recedes─a symbol of the Ondo's fortunate refuge.

pois.name: The Polyleritae District
pois.desc: Here in Amaurot's central district were found the institutions vital to the management of the unsundered star. The ancients employed by these offices were all said to be exceptional practitioners of creation magicks.

pois.name: The Swallowed Spire
pois.desc: Another remnant of ancient civilization, centuries upon centuries of sediment have built up around this tower, leaving only its highest point still peeking out of the rock. How its unburied grandeur might have appeared in its day is a question answered only by one's imagination.

pois.name: The Trinculo Shelf
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a The Tempest.

pois.name: The Workbench
pois.desc: This facility was built by a Crystarium native─a genius artisan seeking to escape from the distractions of the outside world. Although he simply calls the place his “Workbench,” the mundane naming is at odds with the fantastical concept of a forge constructed malms beneath the ocean.

pois.name: Walls of the Forgotten
pois.desc: Grown over by coral and layers of algae, it is believed these remnants were once part of the civilization which ruled the star in the age before the Sundering. The structures themselves have survived millennia without signs of deterioration, and seem impervious to hammer or blade.

pois.name: Where the Dry Return
pois.desc: When the Ondo beheld the coral within this cavern, its crimson branches put them in mind of a land-dweller's veins─thus began the legend that it was a resting place for finless ones who had perished at sea. It was not until recently, however, that folk from the surface learned the reason behind the rather ominous-sounding name.

pois.name: Amaurot
pois.desc: To the depths of the Tempest, to the ocean floor itself, you have come to rescue the Crystal Exarch from the phantom city of Amaurot. But barring your way is the architect of this aetherial construct─Emet-Selch, the Ascian who would lead the First unto destruction. The Light within you strains at its corporeal confines, threatening to break free at any moment. Time does not favor the Warrior of Darkness. You must brave the final days of Amaurot, and confront Emet-Selch in the very midst of this recreated calamity.

pois.name: Akadaemia Anyder
pois.desc: In a quiet corner of Amaurot stands an unremarkable entrance to a most remarkable institution─the Akadaemia Anyder. Within its hallowed halls, the star's ancient overseers toil to perfect the godlike art of creation magicks, their research and experiments bringing into existence myriad forms of fantastical life. Yet even if these creations be naught but reflections of reality─mere phantasms woven from etere─the techniques which engender such miracles are a source of undeniable power. Step now across the threshold, and behold the glories of a civilization lost to the ages.

pois.name: Archons' Design
pois.desc: The city's political and financial center honors the seven individuals whose contributions were instrumental in the founding of Sharlayan. These noteworthy figures were also the inaugural Archons, a title now bestowed in recognition of great achievements.

pois.name: Auk's Landing
pois.desc: Complete with picturesque fountain and ample seating, this modest park is frequented by book readers and poetry reciters. Its name has its origin in the auks that once existed here, a gesture likely lost on the water birds displaced from their colony so many centuries past.

pois.name: Journey's End
pois.desc: Occupying the eastern side of Old Sharlayan, the residential district takes its name from the tale of the city's original settlers. History tells that it is upon this hill, alongside a colony of auks, where the refugees of the great flood chose to build their new homes.

pois.name: Learners' Meet
pois.desc: This public lecture hall in Phenomenon is open to Studium pupils and Sharlayan citizens alike. When prominent professors are scheduled to take the lectern, crowds of aspiring academics and established scholars often fill the room to capacity.

pois.name: Makers' Meet
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Old Sharlayan.

pois.name: Noumenon
pois.desc: The pride of the Studium and parent institution to the Great Gubal Library, this massive collection of scrolls and tomes is the largest of its kind. Knowledge from every corner of the world is collected here, and efforts to compile the ''Bibliotheca Historica''─the ultimate repository of wisdom─is an endeavor without end.

pois.name: Nyunkrepf's Sight
pois.desc: This spur of rock was where the eponymous Archon is purported to have sat when he had matters upon which to meditate. The famous anecdote encourages those frustrated by their studies to linger here in hopes of sudden revelation.

pois.name: Phenomenon
pois.desc: Within the Studium, the central structure of Phenomenon is considered the most historied and the most illustrious. As well as housing auditoriums for both formal lessons and public lectures, it also features the Makers' and Searchers' Meets, known for hosting constant visits from the industrious gleaners.

pois.name: Scholar's Harbor
pois.desc: Although known for its distinctively curving piers, the most prominent feature of the city's port is, without a doubt, the towering statue of Thaliak. Sharlayan's patron deity faces out towards the water, His eternal gaze watching over every vessel which arrives and departs by sea.

pois.name: Searchers' Meet
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Old Sharlayan.

pois.name: The Agora
pois.desc: The Agora was once a simple city square where people gathered to barter for goods. Eventually, enterprising merchants began to construct stalls, and the area evolved into an orderly marketplace.

pois.name: The Baldesion Annex
pois.desc: The Students of Baldesion built their headquarters on the Isle of Val, but as they often found themselves with reason to frequent the city, it was determined that a secondary office was required. So it was that the Annex—and the convenient nap rooms of the andron—became their home away from home.

pois.name: The Confluence
pois.desc: This research facility is known for deciphering the underlying principles of Allagan aetherytes and reconstructing that ancient technology for the modern age. In addition to the production of replacement parts, researchers here are also developing a new, experimental type of eterite.

pois.name: The Forum
pois.desc: In order to accommodate the ninety-nine members of the Forum, the seating in their assembly hall is arranged in the shape of a spiral. Viewed from above, one is reminded of the symbol emblazoned upon the Sharlayan flag─the nautilus shell that keeps the water of knowledge.

pois.name: The Hall of Artifice
pois.desc: This hall houses a lift which descends into the cavernous depths of Labyrinthos. No other method of access is made available for public use.

pois.name: The Last Stand
pois.desc: An eatery established by a pupil who quit the Studium in a rage, incensed by the tasteless meals prepared by an institution lauded for its research into nutrition and culinary arts. In the words of the current proprietor, the cafe is a cultural outpost-the final defense against those who would condemn Sharlayan's diet to blandness and monotony.

pois.name: The Leveilleur Estate
pois.desc: This elegant mansion has stood for three centuries, and is a treasured example of Sharlayan's architectural heritage. For generations, it has served as the home of House Leveilleur─a noble family from which has arisen many distinguished Forum members.

pois.name: The Nymphaeum
pois.desc: A small garden dedicated to legendary spirits of water. In Sharlayan, water is a reminder of the great flood which precipitated the birth of their nation, and a symbol of the knowledge that flows from Thaliak's divine ewer. For this reason is the city populated with an abundance of fountains and other water-based decorative features.

pois.name: The Peristyle
pois.desc: Cargo unloaded from arriving ships is stored here temporarily before being carried off to its final destination. Under the guildship's management, the peristyle also serves as a counter for assigning leves and hunts to dependable agents.

pois.name: The Rostra
pois.desc: This building houses the assembly hall where the Forum debates Sharlayan national policy. Once a simple outdoor plaza, the Rostra would ring with heated discussion through rain, wind, and worse. Following a death by lightning strike, however, plans were drawn up for the imposing stone structure which now crowns Archons' Design.

pois.name: The Scholar
pois.desc: This colossal statue depicts Thaliak, patron deity of Sharlayan. A set of doors at its base lead into a chamber known as the Pathless Way, the interior of which is a mystery to any who has not been inducted into the ranks of the Archons.

pois.name: The Silent Monopteros
pois.desc: In contrast to the Speaking Monopteros, the pupils have an unwritten rule that conversation and disruptive noises are forbidden in this place. It is a spot for quiet reflection, or losing oneself in a good book.

pois.name: The Speaking Monopteros
pois.desc: Found near the entrance to the Studium, this stone arbor is witness to a steady stream of potential spectators. As crowds are often called upon to decide the victor in a debate, pupils have claimed this spot as their preferred arena of argumentation.

pois.name: The Studium
pois.desc: True to its reputation as the cradle of knowledge, Sharlayan is home to numerous private study halls and schooling facilities, but it is the prestigious Studium which represents its foremost institution of learning. The academy opened its doors in the year 432 of the Sixth Astral Era, and for over a thousand years has established a history for producing accomplished Archons and contributing to breakthroughs in every academic field. While initial classes focused on the formal study of the arcane, the occult, and astromancy, it was from these subjects that aetherology─the exploration of magic's fundamental theory─was derived. This signaled the beginning of a more diverse curriculum, the main trunk branching out to include mundane fields such as the natural sciences of astronomy and biology. These were joined by the social sciences (law and economics), the humanities (philosophy and history), the formal sciences (mathematics and statistics), and the applied sciences (alchemy and medicine), and more on the spectrum of learning. Not all faculties are of equal size, however, with some professors teaching only a handful of pupils. This situation is exacerbated by compound disciplines such as somanoutics─combining the study of aetherology, sorcery, and medicine─the introduction of which leads to no few students transferring between faculties during their academy career. Now unburdened by the threat of the Final Days, administrators have seized the opportunity to enact changes. The Studium's post-exodus limitations on accepting foreign students has since been lifted, and hopeful young scholars now converge on the city from every corner of Etheirys.

pois.name: The Thaliak Stoa
pois.desc: This path leads to the harbor's great statue of Thaliak. History tells of the philosophers who gathered here to espouse the merits of a reasoned ungoverned by passion, and are thus credited with the birth of the life word "stoic."

pois.name: Tranquility
pois.desc: Adhering to the philosophy that man thinks his deepest thoughts in natural surroundings, these enchanting woods were chosen as the site for Sharlayan's first private school. Later becoming known as the Studium, the now-legendary institution ensures that its tranquil surrounds are carefully tended and preserved

pois.name: Worldly Affairs
pois.desc: This unassuming post is where applications for entry into Sharlayan are processed. Until recently, the duty-bound nation had maintained strict information protocols, closely scrutinizing the comings and goings of residents and visitors alike with entry records aetherically linked to the citizen registry.

pois.name: Airship Landing
pois.desc: This sturdy pier, originally constructed for flying mounts, was refitted to accommodate the growing popularity of aeronave travel. As well as already serving as a departure point for supplies being flown to Ilsabard, the facilities are being prepared to welcome the arrival of regularly scheduled flights.

pois.name: Alzadaal's Path
pois.desc: This broad avenue begins in the south, leading northeast to the eterite plaza and the bustling heart of the city. Climbing the stairs from Alzadaal's Peace will take one in the opposite direction, towards Paksa's Path and the entrance to Ruveydah Fibers.

pois.name: Alzadaal's Peace
pois.desc: Within this mausoleum is interred the mortal remains of Alzadaal, leader of the Auri tribe which sailed to Thavnair from the mainland. By joining the might of his people with the Arkasodara, Alzadaal tipped the scales against the Gajasura, bringing an end to the internecine war of the Matanga tribes.

pois.name: Artha
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Radz-at-Han.

pois.name: Dharma
pois.desc: Named after the Arkasodara word for "order," Dharma is where word passes into law. It is the home of Radz-at-Han's bureaucracy and judiciary offices, and produces the rules that prevent the independent state from falling into ungoverned chaos.

pois.name: East Balshahn Bazaar
pois.desc: If commerce is the lifeblood of Radz-at-Han, then these roofed market stalls would be its heart. Balshahn himself was a legendary merchant who made a vast fortune through trade with other nations. It was his final wish that his estate be spent on the construction of a great bazaar, ever flowing with coin and wares.

pois.name: Gajasimha Bridge
pois.desc: Built as it is atop a massive outcrop of rock, Radz-at-Han can be entered on foot by this one bridge alone. The structure is named for Gajasimha, a ferocious deity from local mythology described as a gaja crossed with a lion, and known as a vigilant sentinel against the incursion of evil.

pois.name: Hall of the Radiant Host
pois.desc: Radiant headquarters once occupied the area now filled with the stalls and storefronts of the bazaar. Trade became the city's lifeblood, and the business of battle was relegated to this secluded hall far from the haggling merchants.

pois.name: Kama
pois.desc: The largest residential area in Radz-at-Han is represented simply by the Arkasodara term for "love." It is a fitting name for a place where families are born, raised, and nurtured in a harmonious community.

pois.name: Meghaduta
pois.desc: The palace of the satrap serves not only as a residence, but also as the center of Radz-at-Han's government. Meaning “cloud messenger” in the old Arkasodara tongue, Meghaduta was built at the summit of a rocky megalith, its great doors admitting an endless stream of servants, petitioners, and official visitors.

pois.name: Mehryde's Meyhane
pois.desc: Owned and run by the eponymous Mehryde, this meyhane offers light meals and beverages, with the main draw being its myriad varieties of liquor distilled by local alchemists. Foreign visitors are often entranced by the stage performers, whose movements incorporate elements of traditional Thavnairian dance.

pois.name: Nilopala Nourishments
pois.desc: Hamsa were originally reared for the sole purpose of harvesting their venom, until a breeder by the name of Nilopala devised a technique to remove the creatures' toxin glands. The birds suddenly became a viable source of tender, succulent meat, and, before long, Hamsa dishes were considered a staple of Hannish cuisine.

pois.name: Paksa's Path
pois.desc: The paved surface of this city thoroughfare provides passage from the main gate to the district of Dharma. Paksa is the name of an Arkasodara monarch, made famous by the alliance forged with Alzadaal Khan.

pois.name: Ruveydah Fibers
pois.desc: This state-sponsored workshop is famed for producing silk thread of exquisite quality. Its sericulture and weaving techniques were once jealously guarded secrets, but security measures have become lax since Ul'dah and other nations began manufacturing their own silk fabrics.

pois.name: Sundrop
pois.desc: High-ranking foreign delegates gather here to share intelligence, the visits likened to an assembly of stars fallen onto the city. Becoming a center of operations during the Final Days, it was in this room where blasphemy countermeasures were devised and adopted.

pois.name: The Gate of First Sight
pois.desc: Radz-at-Han's main gate is adorned with a sculpture of the national symbol, the all-seeing divine eye keeping watch for those who would enter the city with wickedness in their hearts.

pois.name: The High Crucible of Al-Kimiya
pois.desc: Radz-at-Han's state-sponsored alchemical workshop creates everything from military-purpose coating agents to household detergents, and is constantly researching new compounds and formulae. Similar in pronunciation to the modern word, "Al-Kimiya" is an archaic mainland term for alchemy.

pois.name: The Loyal Rise
pois.desc: Once through the main gate, visitors are greeted by a grand stair before entering the city proper. These same steps are said to have been climbed by the ancestral Arkasodara, Auri, and Hyuran allies upon pledging to uphold the peace and harmony of their newly founded nation.

pois.name: West Balshahn Bazaar
pois.desc: If commerce is the lifeblood of Radz-at-Han, then these roofed market stalls would be its heart. Balshahn himself was a legendary merchant who made a vast fortune through trade with other nations. It was his final wish that his estate be spent on the construction of a great bazaar, ever flowing with coin and wares.

pois.name: Windweft
pois.desc: This mulberry orchard is maintained by Ruveydah Fibers, primarily for the production of leaves to be fed to the silkworms. This is not to say that the remainder goes to waste: the fruit is also edible, while the bark possesses useful medicinal properties. There are few plants considered more valuable in Hannish culture.

pois.name: Yuj
pois.desc: Meaning "bind" in the Arkasodara's classical tongue, this covered walkway sits between the eastern and western halves of the city. The tip of the eterite and the Gate of First Sight can both be spotted from its elevated position.

pois.name: Aporia
pois.desc: The command center coordinating efforts for the great exodus was aptly named after the archaic term for "perplexity." The same word might also apply to the Sharlayans' mindset after learning Hydaelyn's truths, yet it was to face that very challenge that this complex was built.

pois.name: Hatching Canal
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Labyrinthos.

pois.name: Kokkol's Forge
pois.desc: The brightest and boldest engineers in Sharlayan gathered here under the leadership of the brilliantly eccentric Kokkol Dankkol. Heavily involved in the ark's design, his name will ever be known as the man who pioneered the development of the vessel's revolutionary aetherburner.

pois.name: Logistikon Alpha
pois.desc: One of Labyrinthos's three climate control centers, Alpha artificially generates rain and cloud formations by siphoning subterranean water and expelling it as vapor. This technology was devised to enable Sharlayans to alter the atmosphere of an alien star to offer more favorable conditions.

pois.name: Logistikon Beta
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Labyrinthos.

pois.name: Logistikon Gamma
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Labyrinthos.

pois.name: Lower Acrinthos
pois.desc: Located directly below upper Acrinthos, this facility is concerned with the efficient transportation of delivered goods. The cargo lift inside the structure is in constant motion, moving both incoming and outgoing shipments.

pois.name: Meryall Agronomics
pois.desc: In this experimental crop farm, researchers explore agricultural methodology and study the growth of seeds collected from various regions across the world. It is named after Meryall─one of the seven Archons instrumental in Sharlayan's foundation─whose botanical knowledge helped enrich the island's barren soils and resolve food shortages.

pois.name: Mistloom
pois.desc: The technicians here are responsible for overseeing the mist sprayers located throughout Mornveil Forest. Mistloom also regulates the water- and earth- aspected etere transmitted by the elemental reactors in order to maintain optimal humidity levels for the delicate forest environment.

pois.name: Mitato
pois.desc: Researchers here seek to improve upon the traditional techniques of animal husbandry and food preservation. The science behind hams, sausages, cheeses, and butters is rigorously analyzed, and the foodstuffs thus produced are gratefully consumed by Labyrinthos's hard-working inhabitants.

pois.name: Mornveil Forest
pois.desc: A wooded region in the northeast sector of the Outer Circuit. Though manmade, the forest's ecosystem is carefully balanced with the deliberate introduction of insects, rodents, birds, and even a colony of trolls amongst the trees and plant growth.

pois.name: Passemerrant Pasturponics
pois.desc: This research facility was responsible for selecting the most adaptable species of livestock, focusing on resilience, quality of meat versus feed required, and other innate advantages. Passemerrant is counted among the city's seven luminary Archons for his contributions towards domesticating wild animals during the early days of Sharlayan's founding.

pois.name: Phoibos
pois.desc: This facility regulates Labyrinthos's artificial sun, which also shares the name of Phoibos, i.e. "the radiant." Brightness levels are adjusted by time and season to correspond with the climate of southern Ilsabard.

pois.name: Pneuma
pois.desc: Another wind generator, constructed at the same time as Psyche. The Logistikon coordinates these towers, adjusting the speeds of their rotating sails to imitate natural air currents, even mimicking the occurrence of monsoons and other seasonal wind patterns.

pois.name: Psyche
pois.desc: At first glance, this large tower appears no different from an ordinary windmill. However, Psyche—taken from the archaic word for "breath"—does not turn wind into motion, but rather circulates the air with its powerful sails.

pois.name: Sharlayan Hamlet
pois.desc: Located in the Central Circuit, this self-contained settlement provides housing for Forum-authorized researchers. Due to the highly confidential nature of their projects and a strictly enforced information protocol, the men and women here are rarely permitted egress to the city proper.

pois.name: Thaumazein
pois.desc: Thaumazein, or “wonder,” is the emotion one feels at the onset of the quest for knowledge. Such a quest was begun here, in an effort to pierce the mysteries of the aetherial sea, yet what researchers encountered was the will of Hydaelyn Herself. The site became a shipyard, where they would construct an ark destined to reach the very moon.

pois.name: The Aesthete's Tholos
pois.desc: A mineral vault of ores and rough gemstones collected by the gleaners from every region on the star. As preparation for the great exodus, researchers studied these deposits to formulate the most efficient method for mining and refining resources in an alien environment.

pois.name: The Archeion
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Labyrinthos.

pois.name: The Central Circuit
pois.desc: Here in the lowest section of Labyrinthos are found the city's most confidential projects: the Aitiascope, where Sharlayans communicated with the will of the star; and the shipyard, where the ark was built to carry Hydaelyn's hopeful to the moon. Entrance is forbidden to any without the Forum's express permission.

pois.name: The Medial Circuit
pois.desc: This district occupies the middle ring of Labyrinthos, and the facilities here, such as Meryall Agronomics and the mitato, are primarily concerned with research into effective food production. The general populace is not permitted access to areas beyond the Medial Circuit.

pois.name: The Outer Circuit
pois.desc: Following the most fundamental maze design—concentric circles—Labyrinthos resembles a giant mortar, with each successive ring lower than the one before. This district is the outermost of those layers, up near the mortar's rim.

pois.name: The Path of Artifice
pois.desc: This massive lift is one of several which connects the surface of Old Sharlayan to the subterranean research and storage complex of Labyrinthos. At the end of its descent, the mechanism opens up onto the hub of upper Acrinthos, from where passengers or cargo continue onwards towards other facilities.

pois.name: The Phreatic Conduit
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Labyrinthos.

pois.name: The Thirty-third Facet
pois.desc: Serving a dual purpose, this mineshaft was excavated not only to extract ore, but also to continue the gradual development of Labyrinthos. This was the thirty-third such construction project undertaken by Sharlayan to artificially expand the natural hollow left behind by retreating magma.

pois.name: Troglophile's Deep
pois.desc: This cavern serves as a breeding ground for certain subterranean species deemed vital to ongoing research efforts─including a study into creating fertilizer from the subjects' phosphorous-rich excrement. Troglofauna reproduction is, however, an inexact science, routinely resulting in excessive numbers of cave-dwelling offspring spilling out into nearby habitats.

pois.name: Upper Acrinthos
pois.desc: Cargo brought down the Path of Artifice is stacked in this primary storage facility, where neophyte gleaners await to take inventory and deliver supplies to the various facilities. This task is considered training for the guildship's newer members, teaching the best methods for identifying and handling a wide range of shipments.

pois.name: The Aitiascope
pois.desc: Deep in the heart of Labyrinthos lies its secret among secrets─the device through which the Sharlayans have peered into the aetherial sea to learn Hydaelyn's secrets. With their bargain with the Forum fulfilled, the Figli della Settima Alba are poised to journey to the Aitiascope and beyond to beg Her aid, but no depths are without their darkness...

pois.name: Agama Temple
pois.desc: This temple was raised in service of the pilgrims who come to pay their respects at Agama's tomb. An Arkasodara warrior monk, Agama was enshrined as a holy man for his part in quelling the violence between the warring tribes, saving countless lives that would have been lost had he not intervened.

pois.name: Akyaali
pois.desc: This small fishing village is built on the white sands for which it is named. Local fishermen still follow the traditional ways, casting their lines into the shallows from atop stilt-legged platforms, or taking their sturdy boats into deeper waters to trawl with wide-flung nets.

pois.name: Giantsgall Grounds
pois.desc: Quarried here by the wagonload, the purple-streaked stone known as “giantsgall” is one of Thavnair's most coveted exports. Incredibly dense and possessed of high aetherial conductivity, it is prized not only as a building material, but also as a component in the crafting of unyielding arms and armor, and the brewing of alchemical concoctions.

pois.name: Jnanamandapa
pois.desc: Legend has it that this sacred "stage of sagacity" is where the Mrga, who bear a deep affinity with the sea, invited the Manusya (allegedly poor swimmers) to parley and trade heads. Those who worship the Mrga deities are yet known to swim out to the platform as part of their pilgrimage or ascetic rites.

pois.name: Kadjaya's Footsteps
pois.desc: Known as the mother of the Kriegstanz, Kadjaya is honored in both name and form at this open-air stage for dancers. Those who carry on her legacy perform here beneath her stone-carved likeness, strutting and twirling for the glory of their gods and ancestors.

pois.name: Night's Watch
pois.desc: Located near the port town of Yedlihmad, this plateau was used in the manner of a watchtower during a less lawful age in Thavnair's history. Sentinels would be posted here at all hours of the day and night, eyes peeled for the sails of incoming pirates.

pois.name: Palaka's Stand
pois.desc: Named with a traditional word for "guardian," this village is where the stewards of the jungle's shrines and tombs reside. It was originally populated solely by its Arkasodara architects, but as with most places on the island, the inhabitants now include descendants of the mainland settlers.

pois.name: Pavana's Remorse
pois.desc: Pavana was a renowned Arkasodara ascetic who chose the spiritual path after living a life of unspeakable villainy. He meditated daily to purge himself of all ill intent, and the tears he shed during this journey of self-reflection are said to have collected in this jungle pond.

pois.name: Purusa
pois.desc: People once believed that meditating in this temple, dedicated to both Manusya and Mrga, allowed communion with the souls of one's forebears. Those who had lost their path in life would make the pilgrimage to Purusa, seeking to learn ancestral wisdom from the departed.

pois.name: Saltwind's Welcome
pois.desc: As the name implies, this southwestern shore is caressed by a constant breeze of brine-filled air.

pois.name: Svarna
pois.desc: These buildings were once used as storage by a merchant consortium, but after suffering a downturn in business, the premises became the property of Kancana, a job broker based in Yedlihmad. Svarna presently serves as the headquarters for the Hippo Riders and their growing delivery service.

pois.name: Tebqeyiq
pois.desc: More of a sandbar than an island, Tebqeyiq or "the ship's predator" has a reputation for snaring the hulls of unwary helmsmen who fail to account for the shallows' unruly currents.

pois.name: The Font of Maya
pois.desc: This temple was once the abode of an order of Arkasodara ascetics who sought the divine enlightenment of maya. Abandoned for a stronghold deeper in the jungle, the structure now sits derelict and half-submerged in rainwater.

pois.name: The Great Work
pois.desc: Even in Thavnair, the birthplace of alchemy, the practitioners of House Daemir are renowned for the craft of their concoctions. It was they who founded the settlement of the Great Work, and to this day, many talented alchemists choose to reside here and carry on the family's peerless endeavors.

pois.name: The Hamsa Hatchery
pois.desc: This hatchery was once known at home and abroad for the quality of the meat and eggs produced by its hamsa. Abominations emerging from the Tower of Zot, however, brought a ruinous end to both its livestock and its business.

pois.name: The Perfumed Rise
pois.desc: The descriptive name of the hills north of Saltwind's Welcome is attributed to their expansive fields of medicinal herbs. There are those, however, who insist the perfume in question arises from the Great Work nearby.

pois.name: The Shroud of the Samgha
pois.desc: Dense jungle vegetation grows wild and unchecked across a wide band of Thavnair's inland region. Amongst the trees, however, can be found a sprinkling of shrines and temples dedicated to the pantheon of locally worshipped gods─holy sites where once resided the ranks of the faithful.

pois.name: The Wakeful Torana
pois.desc: All those traveling into Radz-at-Han by land must first pass through this stone gateway at the far end of Gajasimha Bridge. In times of need, the entrance can be barricaded in order to protect the city.

pois.name: Ussaqeyiq
pois.desc: This tiny island is in wading distance of Yedlihmad, and is occasionally used as a supply station for seafaring merchant vessels. In the old mainland tongue, its name means "the ship's lover."

pois.name: Yedlihmad
pois.desc: Meaning “new harbor” in a language brought to the island's shores by mainland settlers, Yedlihmad is Thavnair's main port town. Owing to the shallow waters surrounding the island, however, larger trading vessels are forced to anchor at Alnair, and ferry over to the harbor in smaller boats before making their way to Radz-at-Han.

pois.name: The Tower of Zot
pois.desc: Vrtra, great wyrm of the first brood and the hidden satrap of Radz-at-Han, has bid the Scions cross to Narunnair and mount a foray into the tiny island's unnatural spire─a Telophoroi structure known by the locals as the Tower of Zot. Your companions join you on the journey, protective talismans in hand, prepared to face whatever unnamed horrors await you within. Come what may, you cannot allow Nidhana and her kin to perish in the grip of dark magicks and darker designs...

pois.name: Vanaspati
pois.desc: The skies over Thavnair are aflame, and panic spreads through the populace like wildfire. One by one, civilians are twisted into grotesque fiends, hells-bent on slaughtering everything in sight. The deadliest of these creatures leads its newly spawned kin through the jungle, towards a number of smaller settlements, and as such, Ahewann has dispatched his Radiant Host to forestall the carnage. Though Vrtra, too, lends his strength to the cause, even that may prove insufficient, and thus do the Scions enter the fray.

pois.name: Alta Strata
pois.desc: Category:Landmarks

pois.name: Camp Broken Glass
pois.desc: Abandoned when the Telophoroi's schemes plunged the capital into chaos, the village of Laterum was once a checkpoint for travelers as well as being a home to rig workers and their families. The site later became an outpost for the Ilsabard contingent, its members likening the ice cracking constantly underfoot to the sound of broken glass.

pois.name: Cerulea Ingens
pois.desc: A frozen lake lies to the south of the Eblan Rime, its striking blue color caused by the ceruleum spring beneath melting and mixing into the ice above. Of the ceruleum fields which exist in close proximity to the city, Cerulea Ingens is believed to be the largest.

pois.name: Forum Patens
pois.desc: Open plazas such as this one were once popular as a place to gather and relax. Now it lies eerily vacant, a silent witness to the devastation of the capital.

pois.name: Forum Solius
pois.desc: It was in this square that Emperor Solus inspected his troops before embarking upon his second campaign into the Far East. The imperial legions were ultimately successful in their subjugation of the Kingdom of Dalmasca, and officials celebrated the grand victory by transforming the parade ground into a commemorative public park.

pois.name: Horrea Campi
pois.desc: Termed simply "field warehouses" in Garlean, these buildings were filled with grains brought in from the Empire's provinces to be transported into the metropolis as the need arose.

pois.name: Juturna Platform G
pois.desc: This mining platform is designed to pump vast quantities of ceruleum-rich water from the icy depths of Cerulea Ingens. Six more rigs were built within the region for the same purpose, but the eruption of civil war brought all operations to a standstill.

pois.name: Liminal Station IV
pois.desc: The fourth station along the imperial capital's rail network. The name of this stop was intended to represent its tentative position on the threshold of the city, poised to be enveloped by the gradual expansion of Regio Domorum.

pois.name: Monitoring Station G
pois.desc: These family domiciles were built to house the chief and executive officers responsible for overseeing operations of Juturna Platform G. Exclusive to Garlean purebloods, the isolated abode was rarely approached by the provincial workers who labored under its residents' command.

pois.name: Palatium Novum
pois.desc: One of the young Solus's first acts upon becoming Dictator, supreme commander of Garlemald, was to erect a shining landmark in the center of the capital. Once serving as the proud "new palace" of the royal family, the towers now sit scarred and broken amongst the piles of rubble.

pois.name: Regio Domorum
pois.desc: With a steady stream of laborers being ferried in from the Empire's annexed territories, the capital was forced to expand on its edges to contain the growing population. As such, this sprawling residential district was one of the capital's most recent developments.

pois.name: Regio Urbanissima
pois.desc: Here did beat the heart of the Empire─a district pulsing with political, financial, and military authority. Yet these institutions, which once sought dominion over the world, now lie in ruins. Any structure not outright destroyed in the war of succession has been torn apart, its materials cannibalized for the construction of the Tower of Babil.

pois.name: Senaculum Imperialis
pois.desc: Once the center of government for the Republic of Garlemald, this stately building would later house the Emperor's advisory council. Within its walls, countless campaigns were planned and executed─decisions that would result in untold bloodshed, and bring ever greater prosperity to the Empire.

pois.name: Tapper's Den
pois.desc: A small number of laborers dwell here in this natural cave on the edge of Cerulea Ingens. Having miraculously escaped the influence which corrupted so many others, they have survived by extracting—or "tapping "—ceruleum from the lake, which they then burn for warmth or trade for supplies.

pois.name: Tertium
pois.desc: Tertium is the third station along the rail network which serves the imperial capital of Garlemald. Equipped as a dispatch yard with generators and other facilities, it was taken over and fortified by the remnants of the Ist Legion following the city's fall into ruination.

pois.name: The Eblan Rime
pois.desc: Garlean settlers came to this land some eight hundred years ago. Determined to one day return to their homeland in the south, they refuted the permanency of their stay by keeping the area's indigenous name rather than renaming it in their own language.

pois.name: The Enceladeum
pois.desc: This factory complex houses the Empire's foremost facilities for cutting-edge weapons development and warmachina production. While magitek contraptions of all kinds have been manufactured within its walls, its researchers were most recently fixated on perfecting combatants of manlike form.

pois.name: The Pipe
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Garlemald.

pois.name: The Runaway Train
pois.desc: A Mark XLIX passenger train was forced off the tracks by tempered soldiers as it attempted to flee the capital, its twisted bulk left to rust in the ice and snow. Only nobles, high-ranking officers, or citizens with special dispensation were permitted to ride this exclusive service.

pois.name: Victors' Spoils
pois.desc: Former imperial military officers would often move south to the warmer climes of Locus Amoenus, or retire to the capital's outskirts to live in villas such as this one. To thus reap the rewards of one's service was a symbol of one's success, and the goal of many a career soldier.

pois.name: The Tower of Babil
pois.desc: From the ruins of the Garlean imperial palace rises the Tower of Babil, a monstrous edifice constructed by Fandaniel and Zenos's enthralled hordes. While its exact purpose has yet to be ascertained, it is here that the would-be orchestrators of the Final Days await the Guerriero della Luce, who now spearheads a daring mission to infiltrate the tower and vanquish the Telophoroi once and for all.

pois.name: Bestways Burrow
pois.desc: This cavernous abode is home to the Loporrits—the servants created by Hydaelyn to pilot the moon and carry mankind to a new home should the Final Days prove insurmountable. The name "Bestways" represents the Loporrits' aspiration to live up to their chosen appellations to the fullest extent.

pois.name: Greatest Endsvale
pois.desc: The architect of this district envisioned an ideal forest─a place where the new residents of the moon could sit or wander amidst arboreal splendor. The fact that it resembles a forest in only the most abstract sense of the word detracts somewhat from the intended effect. Well, it's the thought that counts...

pois.name: Heimdall's Last Sight
pois.desc: The ancient Allagans launched this Heimdall-class vessel into the heavens to monitor Bahamut's prison, Dalamud. When that colossal satellite awakened around the time of the Seventh Umbral Calamità, the observation craft was shot down as it attempted to halt the activation process.

pois.name: Hoper's Hold
pois.desc: The name seems to be intended as ''Hope''-r's and not ''Hop''-per's Hold, perhaps as pun.

pois.name: Kydonia Knolls
pois.desc: This lifelike face of enormous scale appears to peek out from the surface of Mare Lamentorum. Obviously no natural formation, it is nevertheless unknown who carved this piece, or indeed, whose features it is meant to resemble. One thing is certain: the model would not find the depiction particularly flattering.

pois.name: Lovingway's Darlings
pois.desc: This "flower garden" was lovingly planted by the location's eponymous Loporrit, Lovingway. It appears that the well-intentioned horticulturist misinterpreted the terrestrial references, resulting in a ghastly fungal exhibit to haunt the dreams of all those who behold it.

pois.name: Northern Mare Lamentorum
pois.desc: The northern half of this sizable crater is where the Loporrits make their burrow. The rabbit-like creatures can often be seen scurrying about the landscape, engaged in only Hydaelyn-knows-what manner of inscrutable endeavors.

pois.name: Sinus Lacrimarum
pois.desc: The crater to the southwest of Mare Lamentorum is dominated by a towering eterite. Directly in front of the rotating crystal is the Watcher's Palace, a steadfast sentinel keeping guard over Zodiark's prison.

pois.name: Sinus Tormenti
pois.desc: The impact of a Heimdall-class observation vessel not only created this crater, but also breached an underground bioplant constructed by the Loporrits. The fungal strains they were cultivating spread to the surface, introducing vegetation to the heretofore barren surface of the moon. As to how these varieties evolved into ambulant, sentient fungi, the main theory suggests contact with chimera incubation fluid leaking from the Allagan craft.

pois.name: Southern Mare Lamentorum
pois.desc: The southern side of Mare Lamentorum slopes gently down towards the Cradle of Darkness, with the largely flat terrain doing little to obstruct the sweeping view. The ground is, however, rent asunder by deep canyons, making traversal to the northern side all but impossible on foot.

pois.name: The Biting Brand
pois.desc: The Biting Brand corresponds to the element of Wind and is still intact.

pois.name: The Carrotorium
pois.desc: This district was specifically designed to sustain the continued existence of mankind, and, more importantly, as a wonderful place to cultivate the miraculous orange vegetables known as carrots. Because let's face it: any trial or trouble becomes easier to bear when one holds a carrot in one's paw.

pois.name: The Chlorophosgrot
pois.desc: This cavern is crowded with softly glowing fungi. The phosphorescence illuminates a path to the Chlorophospond, where truly adventurous anglers can indulge in a spot of lunar fishing.

pois.name: The Cradle of Darkness
pois.desc: The ancient primal Zodiark was sealed within this massive hollow, a cradle intended to lull the omnipotent entity into tranquil stasis. Six sword-like monoliths surround the site, but these chains which kept the dark god imprisoned were deliberately shattered by the Telophoroi.

pois.name: The Crushing Brand
pois.desc: The Crushing Brand corresponds to the element of Earth. It has been shattered.

pois.name: The Drowning Brand
pois.desc: The Drowning Brand corresponds with the element of Water. It has been shattered.

pois.name: The Numbing Brand
pois.desc: The Numbing Brand corresponds with the element of Ice. It has been shattered.

pois.name: The Searing Brand
pois.desc: The Searing Brand corresponds with the element of Fire. It has been shattered.

pois.name: The Striking Brand
pois.desc: The Striking Brand corresponds with the element of Lightning. It is still intact.

pois.name: The Watcher's Palace
pois.desc: A structure of enduring design, this brooding tower stands resolute in its vigil of untold millennia. The aetherially conductive plate encircling its spires is reminiscent of a certain architectural style, one found only in the depths of the ocean on the First...

pois.name: Vallis Vulneris
pois.desc: Precipitous chasms radiate from the Cradle like a sunburst, as if the sundered Zodiark's agony had opened jagged wounds in the moon's surface. Whatever the truth of their origin, they present a daunting obstacle to overland travel.

pois.name: Smileton
pois.desc: Smileton was to be a paradise for the people of Etheirys, a refuge where every need is met, its inhabitants content and happy for all their days. But what is happiness? In pursuit of an answer, the Loporrits created the Big Cheese, designed to make manifest all they might need and more to fulfill the needs of their passengers-to-be. They were eager to please─perhaps, too eager─and their plans became more fickle, each new idea a betrayal of the last. The Big Cheese now burrows toward the center of the moon, a labyrinth of contradiction left in its wake. If left unchecked, its wanton pursuit of happiness may very well spell the end of the moon.

pois.name: Anagnorisis
pois.desc: Named for an ancient word meaning “recognition” or “discovery,” this settlement houses those whose job it is to assess the creations admitted to Ktisis Hyperboreia. These observers study every aspect of their charges, and determine if a concept will add to─or detract from─the environ for which it was designed.

pois.name: Easterly Boreneus
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Elpis.

pois.name: Ethoseletikos Boreas
pois.desc: Although relatively small in size, this northern isle is home to Ktisis Hyperboreia, Elpis's foremost facility.

pois.name: Euroneus
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Elpis.

pois.name: First Bloom
pois.desc: A small island welcomes visitors descending the stairs from Propylaion, its fluttering inhabitants offering a first taste of the creative marvels which await them in the environs beyond.

pois.name: Kallimelios Zephyros
pois.desc: This westernmost area of Elpis, composed of a single large isle, is whimsically named for its melodious breeze.

pois.name: Ktisis Hyperboreia
pois.desc: The most extensive facility in Elpis, Ktisis Hyperboreia is a sprawling complex of magically simulated environs. Concepts awaiting evaluation are brought here for the last stages of observation, and, upon meeting the appropriate criteria, are finally released into the world at large.

pois.name: Lethe
pois.desc: Following a process of exhaustive testing, a creation deemed unsuitable for release into the world is brought to this lake, where its life energies are magically unbound and allowed to dissipate. It is at once the most beautiful as well as the most sorrowful locale in Elpis.

pois.name: Metabaseos Thalassai
pois.desc: An annex to Ktisis Hyperboreia, this facility is mainly concerned with the observation and evaluation of sea life. Although its construction appears too narrow to support such an ambitious project, the building's interior harbors six separate marine habitats, each painstakingly recreated via arcane means.

pois.name: Misopses Euros
pois.desc: As particularly unruly creations are allowed to roam these two northeastern isles, Misopses Euros is kept under the strictest oversight.

pois.name: Noetophoreon
pois.desc: A lone tree grows on this small isle found in the southwest of Philomythes Notos, the species of its blossoms said to vary depending on the season and ambient etere conditions. Planted soon after Elpis was constructed, its ephemeral beauty convinced researchers to allow it to grow long after they had concluded their observations.

pois.name: Northerly Zephyrneus
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Elpis.

pois.name: Notoneus
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Elpis.

pois.name: Peripeteia Krystalline
pois.desc: All of Elpis's observational and testing records are archived at this facility, where they are stored in crystal. Its name, meaning "an unexpected twist," is believed to refer to the chaotic revelations contained within its orderly halls.

pois.name: Philomythes Notos
pois.desc: Located in the south of Elpis, this area consists of over half a dozen isles of various sizes, most of which are connected to the central land mass by sturdy spans of worked stone.

pois.name: Poieten Oikos
pois.desc: Beautiful residences line this observation hub nestled in the woods. In addition to being a base for observers, it also serves as a site of conference for taxonomists, whose ofttimes poetic endeavor to name creations earned the hub its appellation.

pois.name: Propylaion
pois.desc: This structure is known as the foregate of Elpis, and houses a teleportation device bound to the main metropolises. Similar facilities were said to be found not only in Amaurot, but in every single region of the ancient world.

pois.name: Southerly Boreneus
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Elpis.

pois.name: Southerly Zephyrneus
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Elpis.

pois.name: The Cthonic Horns
pois.desc: The researchers of this small facility are unlike their colleagues in that they seek to manifest new creations without the aid of creation magicks. Their natural breeding program pairs creatures with differing characteristics, relying purely on chance to conceive heretofore unimagined possibilities.

pois.name: The Hungering Gardens
pois.desc: An observation facility dedicated to dangerous plantlife, be they poisonous, predatorial, or both. Visitors are urged to tread warily, for the garden is mercilessly true to its name.

pois.name: The Mourning Dew
pois.desc: No research is conducted on this isle where observers come to sit and read, or simply stretch out on the warm flagstones. Situated in the east of Philomythes Notos, the etere-rich winds blowing over from Lethe also attract familiars seeking to restore their flagging spirits.

pois.name: The Twelve Wonders
pois.desc: As well as continuing the general duties of observation, this vibrant garden is where Elpis's assorted climates are maintained and adjusted. Should the ambient etere exhibit an excess of any one aspect, aetherial agglomerations of the overabundant element form at the Wonders, allowing for environmental balance to be easily monitored.

pois.name: Ktisis Hyperboreia
pois.desc: The most extensive facility in Elpis, Ktisis Hyperboreia is a sprawling complex of magically simulated environs. Concepts awaiting evaluation are brought here for the last stages of observation, and, upon meeting the appropriate criteria, are finally released into the world at large. Determined not to surrender Meteion, it is within this facility that Hermes has taken refuge, and you and your companions must find and confront him if you are to shed light upon the truth of the Final Days.

pois.name: A-4 Research
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Ultima Thule.

pois.name: Abode of the Ea
pois.desc: A community of those Ea who still cling to their sanity. As the beings are not possessed of corporeal forms, the settlement is completely different from those of creatures of flesh. For instance, rather than houses, they occupy crystals that hold their etere as needed.

pois.name: Absolute Horizon
pois.desc: Situated beneath the dead star at the heart of Ultima Thule, this floating isle is abloom with the first entelechy-the Elpis flower.

pois.name: Ahm Nohl
pois.desc: Standing scattered here are the remains of dragons who were carbonized in an Alphatron attack. Though a hatching ground may be found, those eggs that were fortunate enough to escape destruction spawn only malformed dragonets that cannot long survive. Thus did the area come to be called "a dragonsong, unsung."

pois.name: Base Omicron
pois.desc: A hub of operations for the Omicrons, the mechanical life-forms that call the Alphatron Star home. With its maintenance facilities, weapons stockpile, and tracking systems, the base presents a bleak scene consistent with its military purpose. While there is no leisure to be had, the inhabitants appear welcoming enough to interstellar travelers.

pois.name: Clouded Portal
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Ultima Thule.

pois.name: Elegeia
pois.desc: Etched upon this cluster of stones are the testaments of those Ea who despaired of living and chose to unmake themselves. Many, however, did not leave any words at all, reasoning that it would achieve naught—certainly not the universe's salvation.

pois.name: Empty Portal
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Ultima Thule.

pois.name: Fallow Portal
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Ultima Thule.

pois.name: Hollow of the Flesh
pois.desc: Upon discovering that all life in the universe was doomed, some among the Ea came to yearn for an ephemeral existence once more. These traditionalists developed this facility as a means to reclaim their flesh, but as they had long forgotten their original forms, the endeavor ended in failure. Even now, they continue their experiments in hopes of one day fulfilling their dream.

pois.name: Ostrakon Deka-hexi
pois.desc: This sector is a recreation of the sixteenth civilization encountered by Meteion and her sisters. Although definitive answers remain elusive, it is speculated that the reconstruction echoes the Alphatron Star as it appeared in its last years, or perhaps even an Omicron outpost built upon an invaded world.

pois.name: Ostrakon Deka-okto
pois.desc: This sector is a recreation of the eighteenth civilization encountered by Meteion and her sisters. Ruined and desolate, the world it represents was once the abode of a proud race of dragons who were driven to extinction in a titanic struggle against mechanical invaders from the Alphatron Star.

pois.name: Ostrakon Hena
pois.desc: This sector is a recreation of the first civilization encountered by Meteion and her sisters. The structures are whole, but hauntingly empty─as if all life had come to an abrupt end.

pois.name: Ostrakon Tria
pois.desc: This sector is a recreation of the third civilization encountered by Meteion and her sisters. Known collectively as the “Ea,” the entities which reside here have cast off their corporeal shells and endure eternally in purely spiritual form. An awareness of the universe's inevitable end, however, has blighted their immortal gift with existential misery.

pois.name: Reah Tahra
pois.desc: In the dragons' ancient tongue, the name of this nesting ground may be rendered as "a journey cut short"—a sorrowful reference to the fact that dragonlings had come to be born infirm, if at all, and only extinction awaited their kind.

pois.name: Stigma-1
pois.desc: The prime decision-making authority for an entire machine civilization, this mechanism has been faithfully reconstructed in Ostrakon Deka-hexi. Originally hailed as strategic matrix Alpha-1, catastrophic damage inflicted upon its systems resulted in its currently assigned designation.

pois.name: The Last Dregs
pois.desc: A café jointly operated by the Loporrit Jammingway and the Omicron N-7000. By utilizing Stigma-4's powers of replication, they are able to construct staff and patrons from lost civilizations.

pois.name: The Lost Hydraulic
pois.desc: Once a maintenance platform for conquest weaponry, this hydraulic drifts abandoned but not forgotten.

pois.name: The Nekropolis
pois.desc: The remnants of an extinct civilization re-created by dynamis. Round towers rise up high in the area, with an establishment reminiscent of a bar set into the base of one. The shape of the furnishings suggests that the race who once abided here resembled mankind, but the truth may never be known.

pois.name: The Ragnarok
pois.desc: Due to an as-yet-unexplained quirk of physics, the starship ''Ragnarok'' remains perpetually present at this landing site, despite simultaneously existing at its dock in Old Sharlayan.

pois.name: The Tree of Life
pois.desc: A live specimen collected from a conquered star, this tree is being inexplicably preserved despite having undergone study as per protocol. As the environment from which it hails is vastly different, it requires an intervening device to simply survive, yet it is undeterred from extending out its branches and producing seeds.

pois.name: The Tube
pois.desc: Note: The legendary lush vegetation will only appear for Botanists who have acquired the .

pois.name: The Vitrified Fort
pois.desc: The ruins of an outpost built by Alphatron forces during their invasion of the Dragonstar. Its severely melted state serves as proof of the defenders' fierce resistance.

pois.name: The Wellspring of Regret
pois.desc: Here many an Ea is said to have perished, unable to decide whether to embrace oblivion or endure to regain a vessel of flesh.

pois.name: Unmemoried Portal
pois.desc: Luogo notevole a Ultima Thule.

pois.name: The Dead Ends
pois.desc: Here, at the edge of the universe, await as many stories as there are stars in its sea. Of rises and falls, of beginnings and ends...of a little bird who left home with hope, yet nested in sorrow. Hearken unto these tales to be told...
